"""Machine-readable error contract for ``/api/v1`` — RFC 9457 problem details.

Why a second error shape at all: Q88 already fixed the JSON contract for
``/health`` and for app-nested APIs (``/<slug>/api/*``) and has a test holding
it (``tests/test_176_api_error_contract.py``). Changing that shape would break
frontends that ship today. A brand-new surface, however, gets to pick the
standard one, so ``/api/v1`` answers with ``application/problem+json``:

    {"type": "/errors/not_found", "title": "Not found", "status": 404,
     "detail": "...", "instance": "/api/v1/jobs/x", "code": "not_found",
     "request_id": "..."}

``type`` is deliberately a **relative** URI reference: RFC 9457 allows it, and a
absolute URL would hard-code a hostname into the payload — exactly what Q92
forbids.

Two rules this module exists to enforce:

* the ``detail`` a caller sees never carries request input, exception context,
  stack traces or configuration — see :func:`scrub_detail`;
* codes are stable strings. They are part of the public contract; titles and
  details may be reworded, ``code`` may not.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

PROBLEM_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/problem+json"

# Stable, machine-readable codes. Add here rather than inventing per route.
CODE_INVALID_REQUEST = "invalid_request"
CODE_UNAUTHORIZED = "unauthorized"
CODE_FORBIDDEN = "forbidden"
CODE_NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
CODE_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED = "method_not_allowed"
CODE_CONFLICT = "conflict"
CODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE = "payload_too_large"
CODE_UNPROCESSABLE = "unprocessable_request"
CODE_RATE_LIMITED = "rate_limited"
CODE_INTERNAL = "internal_error"
CODE_READ_ONLY = "read_only"
CODE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE = "service_unavailable"

# Specific causes (EXT-02). These exist because the generic code above told the
# caller *that* it failed without telling them *what to do*: `conflict` covered
# "top up credit", "request a new quote" and "your client reused a key with a
# different body" — three problems with three different fixes.
#
# Note what is deliberately NOT split: 401. Every credential failure keeps one
# code, because separate codes for "unknown key" and "wrong secret" turn the
# endpoint into an oracle for guessing key ids.
CODE_MISSING_SCOPE = "missing_scope"
CODE_TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED = "tool_not_allowed"
CODE_INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT = "insufficient_credit"
CODE_PRICE_CHANGED = "price_changed"
CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT = "idempotency_conflict"
CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS = "idempotency_in_progress"
CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED = "quote_expired"
CODE_QUOTE_INVALID = "quote_invalid"
CODE_CONCURRENCY_LIMITED = "concurrency_limited"
CODE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED = "quota_exceeded"

_TITLES = {
    CODE_INVALID_REQUEST: "Invalid request",
    CODE_UNAUTHORIZED: "Unauthorized",
    CODE_FORBIDDEN: "Forbidden",
    CODE_NOT_FOUND: "Not found",
    CODE_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: "Method not allowed",
    CODE_CONFLICT: "Conflict",
    CODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE: "Payload too large",
    CODE_UNPROCESSABLE: "Unprocessable request",
    CODE_RATE_LIMITED: "Too many requests",
    CODE_INTERNAL: "Internal error",
    CODE_READ_ONLY: "Read-only mode",
    CODE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: "Service unavailable",
    CODE_MISSING_SCOPE: "Missing scope",
    CODE_TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED: "Tool not allowed",
    CODE_INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT: "Insufficient credit",
    CODE_PRICE_CHANGED: "Price changed",
    CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT: "Idempotency conflict",
    CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS: "Request still in progress",
    CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED: "Quote expired",
    CODE_QUOTE_INVALID: "Quote invalid",
    CODE_CONCURRENCY_LIMITED: "Too many concurrent jobs",
    CODE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED: "Quota exceeded",
}

_STATUS_CODES = {
    400: CODE_INVALID_REQUEST,
    401: CODE_UNAUTHORIZED,
    403: CODE_FORBIDDEN,
    404: CODE_NOT_FOUND,
    405: CODE_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED,
    409: CODE_CONFLICT,
    413: CODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,
    422: CODE_UNPROCESSABLE,
    429: CODE_RATE_LIMITED,
    500: CODE_INTERNAL,
    503: CODE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
}

# What a caller is told when the server hit something unexpected. Never the
# exception text: provider SDKs put credentials and customer data in there.
GENERIC_INTERNAL_DETAIL = "The server could not complete this request."


def scrub_detail(value):
    """Return ``value`` with unsafe validation fields removed, JSON-safe.

    Pydantic error entries carry the original request under ``input`` and the
    raised exception under ``ctx``. The first can echo customer content back to
    whoever triggered the error; the second is not serializable at all. Both are
    dropped here so no route has to remember to do it.
    """
    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [scrub_detail(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(key): scrub_detail(item) for key, item in value.items()
                if key not in {"input", "ctx"}}
    return str(value)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ApiProblem:
    """One RFC 9457 problem document."""

    status: int
    code: str
    title: str = ""
    detail: object = ""
    instance: str = ""
    request_id: str = ""
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        code = self.code or _STATUS_CODES.get(int(self.status), CODE_INTERNAL)
        body = {
            "type": f"/errors/{code}",
            "title": self.title or _TITLES.get(code, "Error"),
            "status": int(self.status),
            "code": code,
        }
        detail = scrub_detail(self.detail)
        if detail not in (None, ""):
            body["detail"] = detail
        if self.instance:
            body["instance"] = self.instance
        if self.request_id:
            body["request_id"] = self.request_id

        # Phân loại thử-lại đi kèm chính phản hồi, không nằm riêng trong tài
        # liệu. Trước đây `error_registry` biết đủ cả — lỗi này thử lại được
        # không, và thử lại có phải dùng lại `Idempotency-Key` không — nhưng
        # thứ duy nhất khách nhận được là một mã lỗi. Nên mỗi tích hợp phải tự
        # đoán, và đoán sai theo hướng "thử lại đi" là cách một lần gián đoạn
        # biến thành hai lần tính tiền.
        from platform_core.public_api import error_registry

        #  chứ không phải : hàm kia cố tình ném lỗi cho mã chưa
        # khai, và một mã lạ không được phép biến phản hồi lỗi thành lỗi 500.
        spec = error_registry.REGISTRY.get(code)
        if spec is not None:
            body["retry"] = spec.retry
            if spec.reuse_idempotency_key:
                body["reuse_idempotency_key"] = True

        for key, value in (self.extra or {}).items():
            if key not in body:
                body[key] = scrub_detail(value)
        return body


class ApiError(Exception):
    """Raise inside a ``/api/v1`` handler to answer with a problem document."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, detail: object = "", *,
                 title: str = "", extra: dict | None = None):
        self.status = int(status)
        self.code = str(code)
        self.title = title or _TITLES.get(self.code, "Error")
        self.detail = detail
        self.extra = dict(extra or {})
        super().__init__(f"{self.status} {self.code}")

    def problem(self, *, instance: str = "", request_id: str = "") -> ApiProblem:
        return ApiProblem(
            status=self.status, code=self.code, title=self.title,
            detail=self.detail, instance=instance, request_id=request_id,
            extra=self.extra,
        )


def problem_for_status(status: int, detail: object = "", *, instance: str = "",
                       request_id: str = "") -> ApiProblem:
    """Map a framework status (404 from routing, 405, …) onto the contract."""
    code = _STATUS_CODES.get(int(status), CODE_INTERNAL)
    if int(status) >= 500:
        detail = GENERIC_INTERNAL_DETAIL
    return ApiProblem(status=int(status), code=code, detail=detail,
                      instance=instance, request_id=request_id)


def invalid_request(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(400, CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, detail, extra=extra or None)


def unauthorized(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(401, CODE_UNAUTHORIZED, detail)


def forbidden(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(403, CODE_FORBIDDEN, detail)


def not_found(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(404, CODE_NOT_FOUND, detail)


def conflict(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(409, CODE_CONFLICT, detail, extra=extra or None)


def payload_too_large(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(413, CODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, detail, extra=extra or None)


def rate_limited(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(429, CODE_RATE_LIMITED, detail, extra=extra or None)


def read_only(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    """Emergency switch answer: reads keep working, writes stop."""
    return ApiError(503, CODE_READ_ONLY, detail,
                    title=_TITLES[CODE_READ_ONLY])


def service_unavailable(detail: object = "", *, retry_after: int = 0,
                        **extra) -> ApiError:
    """Temporarily cannot serve this — come back. The code already existed in
    the registry; until EXT-14 nothing constructed it, because the only 503 the
    platform could raise was the global read-only switch."""
    if retry_after:
        extra = {**extra, "retry_after": int(retry_after)}
    return ApiError(503, CODE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, detail,
                    title=_TITLES[CODE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE],
                    extra=extra or None)


# ── Specific causes (EXT-02) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Same statuses as the generic helpers they replace; only the code and the
# advice change. A caller matching on status keeps working.

def missing_scope(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(403, CODE_MISSING_SCOPE, detail, extra=extra or None)


def tool_not_allowed(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(403, CODE_TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED, detail, extra=extra or None)


def insufficient_credit(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(409, CODE_INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT, detail, extra=extra or None)


def price_changed(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(409, CODE_PRICE_CHANGED, detail, extra=extra or None)


def idempotency_conflict(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(409, CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, detail, extra=extra or None)


def idempotency_in_progress(detail: object = "", **extra) -> ApiError:
    """The first attempt is still running — the opposite of a permanent error.

    Sharing `conflict` with the different-body case told a client to give up on
    a request that was about to succeed.
    """
    return ApiError(409, CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS, detail,
                    extra=extra or None)


def quote_expired(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(400, CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED, detail)


def quote_invalid(detail: object = "") -> ApiError:
    return ApiError(400, CODE_QUOTE_INVALID, detail)

"""Runnable examples, generated from the contract rather than written twice.

Every snippet a developer copies — the quickstart, the per-tool recipe, the
n8n node body — is built here from the same :class:`PublicTool` the API
validates against. That is the only way an example cannot drift: there is no
second copy of the payload to forget to update.

Environment variables are part of the contract too, so they are named once:

    LTT_BASE_URL    where the API lives, e.g. https://app.lttstudios.com
    LTT_API_KEY     the developer key, ltt_sk_…
    LTT_PROJECT_ID  optional; only useful for a caller juggling several
                    integrations, since the key already decides the project

No snippet ever contains a key. They read the environment, and the tests refuse
anything that looks like a literal credential.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

ENV_API_KEY = "LTT_API_KEY"
ENV_BASE_URL = "LTT_BASE_URL"
ENV_PROJECT_ID = "LTT_PROJECT_ID"

#: What a caller must set before anything works, and what each one is for.
ENV_VARS = (
    (ENV_BASE_URL, "https://app.lttstudios.com",
     "Where the API lives. No trailing slash; /api/v1 is added for you."),
    (ENV_API_KEY, "ltt_sk_…",
     "Your developer key. Create it in the portal; it is shown once."),
    (ENV_PROJECT_ID, "",
     "Optional. The key already belongs to a project — set this only if your "
     "own code routes by project."),
)

#: How to set them, per shell. People paste the wrong one constantly.
SHELL_EXPORTS = (
    ("bash / zsh (macOS, Linux)",
     'export LTT_BASE_URL="https://app.lttstudios.com"\n'
     'export LTT_API_KEY="ltt_sk_…"'),
    ("PowerShell (Windows)",
     '$env:LTT_BASE_URL = "https://app.lttstudios.com"\n'
     '$env:LTT_API_KEY  = "ltt_sk_…"'),
    ("cmd.exe (Windows)",
     'set LTT_BASE_URL=https://app.lttstudios.com\n'
     'set LTT_API_KEY=ltt_sk_…'),
)


def example_input(tool) -> dict:
    """A payload built from the tool's own declared examples.

    A required parameter with no declared example gets a typed placeholder
    rather than an invented value: a made-up prompt reads like advice, and
    ``<string>`` reads like the instruction it is.
    """
    schema = tool.input_schema
    required = set(schema.get("required", ()))
    payload: dict = {}
    for name, spec in (schema.get("properties") or {}).items():
        examples = spec.get("examples") or []
        if examples:
            payload[name] = examples[0]
        elif name in required:
            payload[name] = f"<{spec.get('type', 'string')}>"
    return payload


def _json(payload) -> str:
    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)


def curl_quote(tool) -> str:
    return (f'curl -X POST "${ENV_BASE_URL}/api/v1/quotes" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ENV_API_KEY}" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'
            f"  -d '{_json({'tool': tool.name, 'input': example_input(tool)})}'")


def curl_submit(tool) -> str:
    """The chargeable call. The Idempotency-Key is not optional decoration."""
    return (f'curl -X POST "${ENV_BASE_URL}/api/v1/jobs" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ENV_API_KEY}" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \\\n'
            f"  -d '{_json({'tool': tool.name, 'quote': '<quote from the step above>', 'input': example_input(tool)})}'")


def python_snippet(tool) -> str:
    payload = _json(example_input(tool)).replace("\n", "\n    ")
    return f'''import os, time, uuid, urllib.request, json

BASE = os.environ["{ENV_BASE_URL}"].rstrip("/") + "/api/v1"
HEAD = {{"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["{ENV_API_KEY}"],
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        # BAT BUOC. Cloudflare tra 403 cho User-Agent mac dinh cua urllib
        # TRUOC khi request toi duoc may chu. Do 24/08: urllib mac dinh -> 403;
        # requests / openai / anthropic / curl / Go / node-fetch deu -> 401,
        # tuc chi rieng urllib bi chan. Dat bat cu ten nao cung qua.
        "User-Agent": "my-app/1.0"}}


def call(method, path, body=None, extra=None):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    request = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, method=method,
                                     headers={{**HEAD, **(extra or {{}})}})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())


payload = {payload}

quote = call("POST", "/quotes", {{"tool": "{tool.name}", "input": payload}})
print("costs", quote["credit"], "credit")

# The same key on every retry of THIS call: a timeout you retry without one is
# a second job and a second charge.
job = call("POST", "/jobs",
           {{"tool": "{tool.name}", "quote": quote["quote"], "input": payload}},
           {{"Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())}})

while job["status"] in ("queued", "running"):
    time.sleep(2)
    job = call("GET", "/jobs/" + job["id"])
print(job["status"], job.get("outputs"))'''


def typescript_snippet(tool) -> str:
    payload = _json(example_input(tool)).replace("\n", "\n  ")
    return f'''const BASE = `${{process.env.{ENV_BASE_URL}}}/api/v1`;
const HEAD = {{
  Authorization: `Bearer ${{process.env.{ENV_API_KEY}}}`,
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
}};

async function call(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown,
                    extra: Record<string, string> = {{}}) {{
  const response = await fetch(BASE + path, {{
    method, headers: {{ ...HEAD, ...extra }},
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  }});
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(await response.text());
  return response.json();
}}

const input = {payload};

const quote = await call("POST", "/quotes", {{ tool: "{tool.name}", input }});
let job = await call("POST", "/jobs",
  {{ tool: "{tool.name}", quote: quote.quote, input }},
  {{ "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID() }});

while (job.status === "queued" || job.status === "running") {{
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000));
  job = await call("GET", `/jobs/${{job.id}}`);
}}
console.log(job.status, job.outputs);'''


def raw_http_snippet(tool) -> str:
    """For anyone whose tool speaks HTTP and nothing else — n8n, Make, curl in
    a language nobody here has heard of."""
    body = _json({"tool": tool.name, "quote": "<quote>",
                  "input": example_input(tool)})
    return (f"POST /api/v1/jobs HTTP/1.1\n"
            f"Host: app.lttstudios.com\n"
            f"Authorization: Bearer <{ENV_API_KEY}>\n"
            f"Content-Type: application/json\n"
            f"Idempotency-Key: 8f14e45f-ea0b-4b3f-8c1a-0f9d2e6c7a10\n"
            f"\n{body}")


def powershell_snippet(tool) -> str:

    return f'''$base = "$env:{ENV_BASE_URL}/api/v1"
$head = @{{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:{ENV_API_KEY}" }}
$input = @'
{payload}
'@ | ConvertFrom-Json

$quote = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$base/quotes" -Headers $head `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body (@{{ tool = "{tool.name}"; input = $input }} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8)

$head["Idempotency-Key"] = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()
$job = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$base/jobs" -Headers $head `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body (@{{ tool = "{tool.name}"; quote = $quote.quote; input = $input }} |
         ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8)
$job.id'''


#: Integrations that speak HTTP without code. Each entry is (name, how).
NO_CODE_RECIPES = (
    ("n8n — HTTP Request node",
     "Method POST, URL `{{$env.LTT_BASE_URL}}/api/v1/jobs`, Authentication "

     "`Bearer {{$env.LTT_API_KEY}}`. Add a header `Idempotency-Key` set to an "
     "expression that is stable for one logical call — `{{$json.orderId}}` is "

     "failed modules by default, which is safe here only because the key is "
     "constant per call — take it from the bundle, never from a timestamp."),
    ("Any HTTP client",
     "Two calls: POST /api/v1/quotes to learn the price, POST /api/v1/jobs "

# ── The synchronous door: POST /chat/completions (Q106) ──────────────────────
#
# Why this door gets its own set of examples. The job door is three steps —
# quote, submit, poll. The chat door is *one*, has no quote at all, and returns
# the bill in the same response. Reusing the job examples here would teach a
# caller to ask for a quote that does not exist.
#
# MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-08-23, openai 2.30.0):
#
#     OpenAI(...).chat.completions.create(...)                    -> 400
#     ... create(..., extra_headers={"Idempotency-Key": ...})     -> 200
#
# The OpenAI SDK *does* generate an idempotency key for every POST and reuses it
# across its own retries — but it only sends one when `_idempotency_header` is
# set, and on the OpenAI client that attribute is `None`. The key is generated
# and then thrown away.
#
# So every example below carries the header. A "cleaner" example without it is
# an example that does not run, and the reader concludes the API is broken
# rather than that the example is wrong.

CHAT_MODEL = "ltt_llm"
CHAT_PATH = "/chat/completions"

#: Deliberately short. A long prompt pulls attention onto its content instead of
#: onto the shape of the call, which is the only thing these examples teach.
CHAT_PROMPT = "Say hello in one sentence."
CHAT_MESSAGES = [{"role": "user", "content": CHAT_PROMPT}]


def _chat_body(max_tokens: int = 300) -> dict:
    return {"model": CHAT_MODEL, "messages": CHAT_MESSAGES, "max_tokens": max_tokens}


def curl_chat() -> str:
    return (f'curl -X POST "${ENV_BASE_URL}/api/v1{CHAT_PATH}" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ENV_API_KEY}" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'
            f'  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \\\n'
            f"  -d '{_json(_chat_body())}'")


def openai_python_chat() -> str:
    """As close to "point the SDK at us" as it gets — and the one line to add."""
    return (
        "# pip install openai\n"
        "import os, uuid\n"
        "from openai import OpenAI\n"
        "\n"
        "client = OpenAI(\n"
        f'    api_key=os.environ["{ENV_API_KEY}"],\n'
        f'    base_url=os.environ["{ENV_BASE_URL}"].rstrip("/") + "/api/v1",\n'
        ")\n"
        "\n"
        "answer = client.chat.completions.create(\n"
        f'    model="{CHAT_MODEL}",\n'
        f'    messages=[{{"role": "user", "content": "{CHAT_PROMPT}"}}],\n'
        "    max_tokens=300,\n"
        "    # REQUIRED. The OpenAI SDK does not send this header for you, so\n"
        "    # leaving it out is a 400. Generate it ONCE per call and reuse the\n"
        "    # same value on every retry of that call: it is what stops a network\n"
        "    # timeout from buying the same generation twice.\n"
        '    extra_headers={"Idempotency-Key": uuid.uuid4().hex},\n'
        ")\n"
        "\n"
        "print(answer.choices[0].message.content)\n"
        'print("charged:", answer.model_extra["x_ltt"]["credit_charged"], "credit")\n'
        "\n"
        "# Do NOT put the key in the client's default_headers. That makes it one\n"
        "# key for every call, and it fails in two ways: a different prompt gets\n"
        "# 409, and an identical prompt silently returns the FIRST answer again\n"
        "# without running anything. The key belongs to a call, not to a client."
    )


def openai_typescript_chat() -> str:
    return (
        "// npm i openai\n"
        'import OpenAI from "openai";\n'
        'import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";\n'
        "\n"
        "const client = new OpenAI({\n"
        f"  apiKey: process.env.{ENV_API_KEY},\n"
        f"  baseURL: `${{process.env.{ENV_BASE_URL}}}/api/v1`,\n"
        "});\n"
        "\n"
        "const answer = await client.chat.completions.create(\n"
        "  {\n"
        f'    model: "{CHAT_MODEL}",\n'
        f'    messages: [{{ role: "user", content: "{CHAT_PROMPT}" }}],\n'
        "    max_tokens: 300,\n"
        "  },\n"
        "  // REQUIRED — the SDK does not send this header for you. One key per\n"
        "  // call, reused unchanged on every retry of that same call.\n"
        '  { headers: { "Idempotency-Key": randomUUID() } },\n'
        ");\n"
        "\n"
        "console.log(answer.choices[0].message.content);\n"
        'console.log("charged:", (answer as any).x_ltt.credit_charged, "credit");'
    )


def python_chat_snippet() -> str:
    """No dependencies, for anyone who would rather not add one."""
    return (
        "import os, uuid, json, urllib.request\n"
        "\n"
        f'BASE = os.environ["{ENV_BASE_URL}"].rstrip("/") + "/api/v1"\n'
        "\n"
        "def chat(messages, max_tokens=300, key=None):\n"
        f'    body = json.dumps({{"model": "{CHAT_MODEL}", "messages": messages,\n'
        '                       "max_tokens": max_tokens}).encode()\n'
        f'    request = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "{CHAT_PATH}", data=body,\n'
        '        method="POST",\n'
        f'        headers={{"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["{ENV_API_KEY}"],\n'
        '                 "Content-Type": "application/json",\n'
        "                 # REQUIRED. Cloudflare refuses the default urllib\n"
        "                 # User-Agent with 403 before it reaches us.\n"
        '                 \"User-Agent\": \"my-app/1.0\",\n'
        '                 "Idempotency-Key": key or uuid.uuid4().hex})\n'
        "    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:\n"
        "        return json.loads(response.read())\n"
        "\n"
        f'answer = chat([{{"role": "user", "content": "{CHAT_PROMPT}"}}])\n'
        'print(answer["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])\n'
        'print("charged:", answer["x_ltt"]["credit_charged"], "credit",\n'
        '      "· held:", answer["x_ltt"]["credit_held"])'
    )


def powershell_chat_snippet() -> str:
    return (
        f'$base = "$env:{ENV_BASE_URL}/api/v1"\n'
        "$head = @{\n"
        f'  Authorization     = "Bearer $env:{ENV_API_KEY}"\n'
        '  "Idempotency-Key" = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()   # one key per CALL\n'
        "}\n"
        "$body = @{\n"
        f'  model      = "{CHAT_MODEL}"\n'
        f'  messages   = @(@{{ role = "user"; content = "{CHAT_PROMPT}" }})\n'
        "  max_tokens = 300\n"
        "} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8\n"
        "\n"
        f'$answer = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "$base{CHAT_PATH}" -Headers $head `\n'
        '  -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body\n'
        "$answer.choices[0].message.content\n"
        '"charged: $($answer.x_ltt.credit_charged) credit"'
    )


def raw_http_chat_snippet() -> str:
    return (f"POST /api/v1{CHAT_PATH} HTTP/1.1\n"
            f"Host: app.lttstudios.com\n"
            f"Authorization: Bearer <{ENV_API_KEY}>\n"
            f"Content-Type: application/json\n"
            f"Idempotency-Key: 8f14e45f-ea0b-4b3f-8c1a-0f9d2e6c7a10\n"
            f"\n{_json(_chat_body())}")


def chat_snippets() -> tuple:
    """Every chat-door example, in the order people actually try them."""
    return (
        ("Python — OpenAI SDK", openai_python_chat()),
        ("TypeScript — OpenAI SDK", openai_typescript_chat()),
        ("cURL", curl_chat()),
        ("Python — no dependencies", python_chat_snippet()),
        ("PowerShell", powershell_chat_snippet()),
        ("HTTP", raw_http_chat_snippet()),
    )


#: Where the chat door differs from the job door. Written down rather than left
#: for the reader to trip over, because every one of these has a failure mode.
CHAT_DIFFERENCES = (
    ("No quote",
     "The price depends on how many tokens the model produces, and that number "
     "does not exist when you call. The platform holds a CEILING before it "
     "touches the model and then charges the measured usage, so "
     "x_ltt.credit_charged is usually well below x_ltt.credit_held. If you "
     "need the price before the work runs, use POST /api/v1/quotes and the job "
     "door."),
    ("Idempotency-Key is required, not optional",
     "With no quote it is the only thing standing between a network retry and "
     "paying twice. The OpenAI SDK does NOT send this header for you — add it "
     "per call. Leaving it out is a 400 that says exactly what to do."),
    ("One key per CALL, not per client",
     "A fixed key in default_headers breaks in two ways: a different prompt "
     "gets 409, and an identical prompt silently returns the FIRST answer "
     "again with nothing to show for it. Generate the key right before the "
     "call, and reuse it only when retrying that same call."),
    ("There is a time budget, so there is a max_tokens ceiling",
     "The call has to finish inside the server's synchronous budget, so "
     "max_tokens is capped. Asking for more is refused immediately with a "
     "400 naming the number, rather than cut off half-written. For longer "
     "generations submit the same work to POST /api/v1/jobs, which has no such "
     "ceiling."),
    ("No streaming yet",
     '"stream": true is refused with 400. Accepting it and answering without '
     "a stream would break the SDK somewhere much harder to trace, so the "
     "server says so plainly."),
    ("Busy is 503, not 429",
     "503 means the machine cannot serve right now — you are NOT charged, and "
     "Retry-After says when to come back. 429 means something else entirely: "
     "you are calling too fast, or you hit an account limit."),
)


# ── Plugging a coding CLI into the API (Q107) ────────────────────────────────
#
# The lesson these exist for: what stops a developer is almost never the
# protocol, it is filling in a config file correctly. Two base URLs that differ
# by four characters, a model name that must match exactly, and one environment
# variable that has to be set at user level rather than in a shell — each of
# those is a silent failure with an unhelpful symptom.
#
# 🔴 THE TWO BASE URLs ARE NOT A TYPO. The clients append different suffixes:
#
#     Codex        base_url + "/responses"      -> needs …/api/v1
#     Claude       base    + "/v1/messages"     -> needs …/api
#
#   Swap them and Codex asks for /api/responses (404) while Claude asks for
#   /api/v1/v1/messages (404). Same host, same key, four characters apart.
#
# No snippet here contains a key, for the same reason as every other snippet in
# this module: they read the environment, and the tests refuse anything that
# looks like a literal credential.

#: The model alias a customer types. Deliberately the public alias, never the
#: internal id — a customer who pins to the internal id is a customer we cannot
#: move to a different model later without breaking them (test_212).
CLI_MODEL = "ltt_llm"


def _goc(base_url: str) -> str:
    return (base_url or "https://app.lttstudios.com").rstrip("/")


def codex_config(base_url: str) -> str:
    """`~/.codex/config.toml` — the provider block. Additive; changes nothing else."""
    return (
        "# ~/.codex/config.toml — add this, change nothing above it.\n"
        "# Your existing default `model` stays the default; only\n"
        "# `codex --profile ltt` goes to LTT Studios.\n"
        "[model_providers.ltt]\n"
        'name = "LTT Studios"\n'
        f'base_url = "{_goc(base_url)}/api/v1"   # with /v1 — Codex appends /responses\n'
        f'env_key = "{ENV_API_KEY}"\n'
        'wire_api = "responses"                  # the only value Codex supports\n'
        "stream_idle_timeout_ms = 600000"
    )


def codex_profile() -> str:
    """`~/.codex/ltt.config.toml` — a separate file, and that is not optional.

    Codex 0.145 refuses `[profiles.X]` inside `config.toml` outright:
    *"cannot be used while config.toml contains legacy `[profiles.ltt]` config"*.
    """
    return (
        "# ~/.codex/ltt.config.toml — a SEPARATE file.\n"
        "# Codex 0.145+ refuses [profiles.ltt] inside config.toml.\n"
        f'model = "{CLI_MODEL}"\n'
        'model_provider = "ltt"\n'
        '# Left at its default the model spends most of max_tokens thinking\n'
        '# before it answers.\n'
        'model_reasoning_effort = "low"\n'
        'model_reasoning_summary = "none"\n'
        "model_context_window = 65536"
    )


def claude_code_env(base_url: str) -> str:
    """Claude Code CLI reads plain environment variables."""
    return (
        f'$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "{_goc(base_url)}/api"   # NO /v1 — the client adds it\n'
        f'$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = $env:{ENV_API_KEY}\n'
        f'$env:ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "{CLI_MODEL}"\n'
        f'$env:ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL = "{CLI_MODEL}"   # background work'
    )


def claude_code_settings(base_url: str) -> str:
    """`~/.claude/settings.json` — survives a new terminal."""
    return _json({
        "env": {
            "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": f"{_goc(base_url)}/api",
            "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "<your ltt_sk_… key>",
            "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": CLI_MODEL,
            "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": CLI_MODEL,
        }
    })


def vscode_claude_settings(base_url: str) -> str:
    """Settings the **Claude Code VS Code extension** needs — not the same as the CLI.

    Measured on a clean VM, 2026-08-24: after configuring the CLI correctly, the
    extension still showed a **Sign In** screen. It does **not** pick up
    `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the OS the way the CLI does — a known regression
    since extension v2.0.0 (anthropics/claude-code issues #9010, #38430).

    The extension ships two settings of its own to work around it. Both names
    were read from the installed extension's ``package.json``, not from a blog
    post: an article we checked used ``claude-code.*`` and the real prefix is
    ``claudeCode.*``.

    ``claudeCode.environmentVariables`` is declared ``scope: "machine"``, so it
    only takes effect in **User** settings. Put it in a workspace
    ``.vscode/settings.json`` and nothing happens, with no error.
    """
    return (
        "{\n"
        '  "claudeCode.disableLoginPrompt": true,\n'
        '  "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [\n'
        '    {"name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "' + base_url + '/api"},\n'
        f'    {{"name": "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", "value": "{CLI_MODEL}"}},\n'
        f'    {{"name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value": "{CLI_MODEL}"}}\n'
        "  ]\n"
        "}"
    )


def vscode_codex_config(base_url: str) -> str:
    """Config the **Codex VS Code extension** needs — root level, no profile.

    The extension has no provider settings at all (checked in its
    ``package.json``); it drives the Codex CLI and therefore reads
    ``~/.codex/config.toml``. But it has no way to pass ``--profile``.

    And a profile cannot be selected from the file either. Codex 0.145 rejects it
    outright::

        Error: legacy `profile = "ltt"` config is no longer supported;
               use `--profile ltt` with `ltt.config.toml` instead

    So for the extension the provider has to sit at the **root** of
    ``config.toml``. The trade-off is real and must be stated: this makes LTT the
    **default** for ``codex`` on the command line too, whereas the profile form
    leaves the customer's default untouched.
    """
    return (
        f'# Root level - REPLACES your default model for `codex` too.\n'
        f'# Use the profile form instead if you only want the CLI.\n'
        f'model = "{CLI_MODEL}"\n'
        f'model_provider = "ltt"\n'
        f'model_reasoning_effort = "low"\n'
        f'model_context_window = 65536\n'
        f'\n'
        f'[model_providers.ltt]\n'
        f'name = "LTT Studios"\n'
        f'base_url = "{base_url}/api/v1"\n'
        f'env_key = "{ENV_API_KEY}"\n'
        f'wire_api = "responses"\n'
        f'stream_idle_timeout_ms = 600000\n'
    )


#: Cai bay lon nhat cua phan tien ich, viet ra de khach khoi tu phat hien.
VSCODE_BAY = (
    "The extensions do NOT read OS environment variables the way the CLIs do. "
    "Configuring the CLI is not enough - see the two blocks above.",
    "Restart VS Code completely after any change. `setx` only affects NEW "
    "processes, and on Windows an already-running Explorer hands the old "
    "environment to everything you launch from the Start menu.",
    "Put the Claude settings in USER settings.json, not a workspace one: the "
    "setting is scope:machine and is silently ignored elsewhere.",
)


def claude_desktop_registry(base_url: str) -> str:
    r"""Claude Desktop on Windows: an OS **policy**, not an app config file.

    The app's runtime settings live in Electron's LevelDB and cannot be edited by
    hand. But the **third-party inference** section is read from OS-managed
    policy - a .mobileconfig on macOS, the **registry** on Windows. That is the
    enterprise deployment path and it is stable.

    Until we found this, the Claude Desktop section of our own guide said "manual
    entry only", which was wrong.

    Four rules from the official reference. Each of them fails **silently**:

    * `inferenceGatewayBaseUrl` is the **origin**; the app appends
      `/v1/messages` itself. Shipping `/v1` in the value yields
      `/v1/v1/messages` and a 404 with no other clue.
    * HTTPS is **required** (loopback excepted).
    * Config is read **once at launch**, so the app must be fully quit, not just
      closed to the tray.
    * A policy under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE` makes the app ignore the
      `HKEY_CURRENT_USER` one **entirely**.
    """
    khoa = r"[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude]"
    mo = '[{\\"name\\": \\"' + CLI_MODEL + '\\"}]'
    dong = [
        "Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00",
        "",
        khoa,
        '"inferenceProvider"="gateway"',
        '"inferenceGatewayBaseUrl"="' + base_url + '/api"',
        '"inferenceGatewayApiKey"="<your ltt_sk_... key>"',
        '"inferenceGatewayAuthScheme"="bearer"',
        '"inferenceModels"="' + mo + '"',
        '"modelDiscoveryEnabled"="false"',
    ]
    return "\n".join(dong) + "\n"


def claude_desktop_steps(base_url: str) -> tuple:
    """Claude Desktop does NOT read ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. It has its own form."""
    return (
        ("Open the window",
         "Help → Troubleshooting → Enable Developer Mode, then "
         "Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference…  (on Windows the app menu "

"""Every store that holds customer data, how long it keeps it, and why.

The problem with retention rules that live in constants
-------------------------------------------------------

This platform already ages out job events, request logs and notifications. Each
rule lived next to the code that wrote the rows, which is the right place for
the rule and the wrong place for the *policy*: nobody could answer "what do we
hold about a customer, and for how long" without reading five modules and
hoping there was not a sixth.

There was a sixth. ``api_security_events`` shipped in EXT-16 with a
``purge_expired()`` that nothing ever called — a retention function nobody runs
is a comment, and the table would have grown forever.

So the classes are declared here, in one place, and a **ratchet test** fails when
a table appears without one. Forgetting becomes visible instead of silent.

The classes, and what they mean
-------------------------------

``EVIDENCE``
    Money and permission. Ledger entries, admin actions, pricing versions,
    developer keys. **Never deleted** — not by retention, not by an account
    closing. A refund dispute six months later is answered from these rows, and
    an audit that can be aged out is not an audit.

``OPERATIONAL``
    Useful while fresh, worthless when stale: request logs, job events,
    security events, cost observations, notifications. Aged out on a schedule.

``CONTENT``
    What the customer actually sent and received — uploads and artifacts. The
    largest by far, and the most sensitive. Lifecycle belongs to the storage
    layer and the upload sweeper, not to a row count here.

``DERIVED``
    Rebuildable from the others: the system dossier, generated docs, Postman.
    Losing them costs a command, not a fact.

What is deliberately *not* here
-------------------------------

Legal text. The site already has a privacy policy, terms and a data-deletion
page, and this module links to them rather than restating them — a second copy
of a legal promise is a second promise, and the two will differ.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from platform_core.i18n import N_, _ as _t

EVIDENCE = "evidence"
OPERATIONAL = "operational"
CONTENT = "content"
DERIVED = "derived"
CLASSES = (EVIDENCE, OPERATIONAL, CONTENT, DERIVED)

#: Where the legal wording lives. Links, never copies (see the module docstring).
LEGAL_LINKS = {
    "privacy": "https://lttstudios.com/privacy-policy/",
    "terms": "https://lttstudios.com/terms/",
    "data_deletion": "https://lttstudios.com/data-deletion/",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Store:
    """One place customer data lives, and the promise made about it."""

    table: str
    klass: str
    #: ``None`` means "kept for as long as the account exists".
    retention_days: int | None
    #: Who can read it. Written for a person answering a privacy question.
    readable_by: str
    #: Why it is kept at all. A store nobody can justify is one to delete.
    reason: str
    #: How rows leave. Empty when nothing removes them, which is a claim the
    #: ratchet test checks rather than takes on trust.
    purged_by: str = ""

def translated(store: "Store") -> dict:
    """One row as the privacy page shows it, in the reader's language.

    Resolved here rather than in the template so there is one place that knows
    which fields are prose and which are identifiers — a table name is not
    translated, and translating it would break the only thing that lets a
    customer match this page against their export.
    """
    return {"table": store.table, "klass": store.klass,
            "retention_days": store.retention_days,
            "readable_by": _t(store.readable_by), "reason": _t(store.reason)}


def by_class(klass: str) -> tuple:
    return tuple(store for store in STORES if store.klass == klass)


def store_for(table: str) -> Store | None:
    for store in STORES:
        if store.table == table:
            return store
    return None


#: Tables that hold nothing about a customer, so they need no class. Listed
#: explicitly: "it is not customer data" is a claim worth writing down, because
#: the next person will assume the omission was an oversight.
NOT_CUSTOMER_DATA = frozenset({
    "alembic_version", "platform_info", "api_keys", "api_policies",
    "api_policy_assignments", "api_kill_switches", "app_access",
    "credit_packages", "gpu_leases",
    # Ai đang giữ vai trò chạy việc nền. Máy + pid, không có gì của khách.
    "singleton_leases",
    # Node hạ tầng của CHÍNH TA: IP công khai của gateway, bridge, subnet, dải
    # cổng. Không có `user_id` và không có gì của khách — máy của khách nằm ở
    # `vps_instance`, và bảng đó đã được xếp loại ở trên.
    "vps_gateway",
})


def unclassified(tables) -> list:
    """Tables the inventory does not mention. The ratchet's whole job.

    A new table that holds customer data and slips in unlisted is exactly how a
    platform ends up unable to answer "what do you keep about me" — and the
    honest answer to that question is not one anybody wants to improvise.
    """
    known = {store.table for store in STORES} | set(NOT_CUSTOMER_DATA)
    return sorted(name for name in tables if name not in known)

           "NOT_CUSTOMER_DATA", "OPERATIONAL", "STORES", "Store", "by_class",

"""DB-backed idempotency for chargeable API operations.

The rule this implements: *same key + same request → same logical operation;
same key + different request → conflict.*

Why it cannot be built on ``jobs.dedupe_key``: that one deduplicates only while
the earlier job is still queued or running. A client that retries after its
first attempt already finished — the normal reaction to a timeout it cannot
distinguish from a failure — would get a second job and a second credit hold.

Why the unique constraint does the work: two requests racing with the same key
both attempt an INSERT; the database lets exactly one through and the loser
reads the winner's row. Checking "does a record exist?" first and inserting
afterwards is the classic check-then-write race, and under concurrency it does
double-charge.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from sqlalchemy import select, text
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

from platform_core.public_api.errors import (idempotency_conflict,
                                             idempotency_in_progress,
                                             invalid_request)
from platform_core.public_api.tables import (ApiIdempotencyRecord,
                                             IDEMPOTENCY_COMPLETED,
                                             IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS)

MAX_KEY_LENGTH = 255
MIN_KEY_LENGTH = 8


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def canonical_hash(payload) -> str:
    """Stable fingerprint of a request body, independent of key order."""
    canon = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, default=str,
                       separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(canon.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def require_key(raw: str) -> str:
    """Validate the ``Idempotency-Key`` header.

    Required rather than optional on chargeable routes: making it optional means
    the safe path is the one a client has to remember, and the unsafe one is the
    default. A minimum length keeps "1" or "retry" — values that collide across
    unrelated requests — out of the table.
    """
    key = str(raw or "").strip()
    if not key:
        raise invalid_request(
            "This endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header.")
    if len(key) < MIN_KEY_LENGTH or len(key) > MAX_KEY_LENGTH:
        raise invalid_request(
            f"Idempotency-Key must be between {MIN_KEY_LENGTH} and "
            f"{MAX_KEY_LENGTH} characters.")
    return key


def _lock(db, key_id: str, operation: str, key: str) -> None:
    """Serialise same-key requests on PostgreSQL.

    The unique constraint already makes double-insert impossible; this only
    turns a racing pair into "wait, then replay" instead of "fail, then retry",
    which is the friendlier of the two correct behaviours. SQLite serialises
    writes at the file level, so it needs nothing here.
    """
    if db.bind is not None and db.bind.dialect.name == "postgresql":
        db.execute(text("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(:k))"),
                   {"k": f"public-api-idem:{key_id}:{operation}:{key}"})


def find(db, *, key_id: str, operation: str, key: str):
    return db.execute(select(ApiIdempotencyRecord).where(
        ApiIdempotencyRecord.key_id == key_id,
        ApiIdempotencyRecord.operation == operation,
        ApiIdempotencyRecord.idempotency_key == key,
    )).scalar_one_or_none()


def begin(db, *, key_id: str, user_id: str, operation: str, key: str,
          request_hash: str):
    """Claim the key for this request, or return the record that already owns it.

    Returns ``(record, replay)``. ``replay=True`` means the caller must not do
    the work again and should answer from ``record.response``.

    Raises 409 when the same key arrives with a different payload, and when a
    first attempt is still in flight — a client that fires two different
    requests under one key has a bug, and one that retries mid-flight should
    wait rather than be handed a half-built answer.
    """
    _lock(db, key_id, operation, key)
    existing = find(db, key_id=key_id, operation=operation, key=key)
    if existing is not None:
        return _replay(existing, request_hash)

    record = ApiIdempotencyRecord(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()), key_id=key_id, user_id=user_id,
        operation=operation, idempotency_key=key, request_hash=request_hash,
        status=IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS, created_at=_now(), updated_at=_now(),
    )
    db.add(record)
    try:
        db.flush()
    except IntegrityError:
        # Lost the race (or no advisory lock, as on SQLite). The winner's row is
        # authoritative; roll back only this insert and read it.
        db.rollback()
        existing = find(db, key_id=key_id, operation=operation, key=key)
        if existing is None:      # pragma: no cover - defensive
            raise
        return _replay(existing, request_hash)
    return record, False


def _replay(record, request_hash: str):
    from platform_core.public_api import metrics

    if record.request_hash != request_hash:
        metrics.increment(metrics.IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT)
        raise idempotency_conflict(
            "This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request "
            "body.", idempotency_key=record.idempotency_key)
    if record.status != IDEMPOTENCY_COMPLETED:
        raise idempotency_in_progress(
            "A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed.",
            idempotency_key=record.idempotency_key)
    return record, True


def complete(db, record, *, response: dict, job_id: str = "") -> None:
    """Store the logical answer so a later retry replays it byte for byte."""
    record.status = IDEMPOTENCY_COMPLETED
    record.response = dict(response or {})
    record.job_id = str(job_id or "")
    record.updated_at = _now()
    db.flush()


#: The retry window a client could plausibly still be in. Past it, the record
#: protects nothing — and it holds a stored response body, so keeping it longer
#: is keeping a copy of somebody's data for no reason.
RETENTION_DAYS = 7


def purge_expired(db, *, days: int = RETENTION_DAYS,
                  now: datetime | None = None) -> int:
    """Drop idempotency records past the retry window. Caller commits.

    Only completed ones: an in-flight record is what stops a concurrent retry
    from opening a second job, and removing it mid-call would reintroduce the
    double charge this table exists to prevent.
    """
    cutoff = (now or _now()) - timedelta(days=max(1, int(days)))
    rows = db.execute(select(ApiIdempotencyRecord).where(
        ApiIdempotencyRecord.created_at < cutoff,
        ApiIdempotencyRecord.status != IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS,
    )).scalars().all()
    for row in rows:
        db.delete(row)
    return len(rows)

"""Turning a public tool call into a real job: validate → price → hold → queue.

This module is the adapter Q92 promised. It owns no engine of its own: pricing
is ``registry.credit_for()``, the queue is the ``jobs`` table, the money is the
credit ledger, and the atomicity comes from ``job_submit.submit_with_credit()``
— all of which the UI has been using in production.

**Order is the contract** (COMMON_RULES §5), and it is enforced here rather than
per route:

    validate input → resolve the quote → hold credit → insert the job
                                         └── one transaction, caller commits ──┘

Validation before money means a typo cannot cost anything. The hold and the job
row commit together, so "credit held but no job" cannot survive a crash: there
is no second store to fall out of sync with, and no queue signal outside the
database (Q26). Whatever the crash, either both rows are there or neither is.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from platform_core.public_api.errors import invalid_request

# Media parameters take an upload/artifact id. Resolving one to a storage key is
# Prompt 07's job; until then a tool that needs media simply cannot be called,
# which is better than inventing a half-contract now.
_MEDIA_TYPES = {"image", "image[]", "video", "video[]", "audio"}

# Internal params the platform adds for its own bookkeeping. The prefix keeps
# them out of the public contract and makes them greppable.
API_META_KEY = "_api"


def _field_error(field: str, message: str):
    return invalid_request(f"{field}: {message}", field=field)


def validate_public_input(tool, payload: dict) -> dict:
    """Check a caller's input against the published contract. Returns it clean.

    Unknown fields are **rejected**, not ignored. The published schema says
    ``additionalProperties: false``; silently dropping a misspelled parameter
    would let a customer pay for a job that quietly ignored what they asked for.
    """
    if payload is None:
        payload = {}
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise invalid_request("input must be an object.")

    schema = tool.input_schema
    properties = schema.get("properties", {})
    unknown = sorted(set(payload) - set(properties))
    if unknown:
        raise invalid_request(
            f"Unknown input field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}.", fields=unknown)

    missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", ())
               if payload.get(name) in (None, "")]
    if missing:
        raise invalid_request(
            f"Missing required field(s): {', '.join(missing)}.", fields=missing)

    clean: dict = {}
    for name, value in payload.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        spec = properties[name]
        clean[name] = _validate_value(name, value, spec)
    return clean


def _validate_value(name: str, value, spec: dict):
    kind = spec.get("type")
    if kind == "integer":
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be an integer.")
    elif kind == "number":
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be a number.")
    elif kind == "boolean":
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be a boolean.")
    elif kind == "array":
        if not isinstance(value, list):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be an array.")
    elif kind == "object":
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be an object.")
    else:
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise _field_error(name, "must be a string.")

    allowed = spec.get("enum")
    if allowed is not None and value not in allowed:
        raise _field_error(name, f"must be one of: {', '.join(map(str, allowed))}.")
    if "minimum" in spec and value < spec["minimum"]:
        raise _field_error(name, f"must be >= {spec['minimum']}.")
    if "maximum" in spec and value > spec["maximum"]:
        raise _field_error(name, f"must be <= {spec['maximum']}.")
    if "maxLength" in spec and isinstance(value, str) and len(value) > spec["maxLength"]:
        raise _field_error(name, f"must be at most {spec['maxLength']} characters.")
    return value


def tool_contract(tool) -> dict:
    """The app's public contract for this tool, as declared in its manifest."""
    from platform_core.registry import discover

    for item in discover():
        if item.manifest.slug != tool.app_slug:
            continue
        for spec in item.manifest.tools:
            if spec.job_type == tool.job_type and (
                    spec.name == tool.name
                    or (spec.api_contract or {}).get("public_name") == tool.name):
                return dict(spec.api_contract or {})
    return {}


def media_params(tool) -> dict:
    """``param -> internal media type`` for the tool's published inputs."""
    from platform_core.registry import discover

    internal_schema = _internal_schema(tool, discover())
    published = set((tool.input_schema or {}).get("properties", {}))
    return {name: str(spec.get("type"))
            for name, spec in internal_schema.items()
            if name in published and str(spec.get("type")) in _MEDIA_TYPES}


def build_job_params(tool, clean_input: dict, *, media_values=None) -> dict:
    """Map validated public input onto the internal job parameters.

    Two translations happen here and nowhere else: a public model alias becomes
    the real model id, and a media reference becomes a storage key. Both exist
    so the public contract can stay stable while the implementation changes.

    ``media_values`` carries what a media parameter should become. At quote time
    it is a placeholder (nothing has been promoted yet — Q85 forbids persisting
    an input before its job holds credit); at submit time it is the promoted
    key. A media parameter with no value at all is refused rather than silently
    dropped.
    """
    from platform_core.registry import discover

    internal_schema = _internal_schema(tool, discover())
    supplied = dict(media_values or {})
    params: dict = {}

    # A hidden parameter means "the server decides", and the server's decision is
    # the default the app declared. Leaving it out entirely is not the same
    # thing: the handler then falls back to *its* default, which is a different
    # value in at least one real case — hiding `operation` on the storyboard tool
    # made it run (and price) as the prompt-package generator instead.
    hidden = {str(name) for name in ((tool_contract(tool).get("hidden")) or ())}
    for name in hidden:
        spec = internal_schema.get(name) or {}
        if "default" in spec and name not in clean_input:
            params[name] = spec["default"]

    for name, value in clean_input.items():
        kind = str((internal_schema.get(name) or {}).get("type") or "string")
        if kind == "model_ref":
            resolved = tool.resolve_model(value)
            if not resolved:
                raise _field_error(name, "unknown model alias.")
            params[name] = resolved
        elif kind in _MEDIA_TYPES:
            if name not in supplied:
                raise _field_error(name, "this input requires an upload id.")
            params[name] = supplied[name]
        else:
            params[name] = value
    return params


def promote_media(db, storage, *, job, sessions: dict) -> list:
    """Move confirmed uploads to their durable keys, after the hold exists.

    Order is Q85's, not a preference: the credit hold proves the job is real
    before anything becomes permanent in storage. Returns the promotions so the
    caller can compensate them if its transaction later fails — object storage
    does not roll back with the database.
    """
    from sqlalchemy.orm.attributes import flag_modified
    from platform_core import upload_sessions

    promotions: list = []
    params = dict(job.params or {})
    for param, session in sessions.items():
        suffix = _suffix(session.filename)
        final_key = f"{job.app_slug}/{job.user_id}/{job.id}/{param}{suffix}"
        key = upload_sessions.promote(db, storage, session, job=job,
                                      final_key=final_key)
        promotions.append((session.staging_key, final_key, session.content_type))
        params[param] = key
    job.params = params
    flag_modified(job, "params")
    db.flush()
    return promotions


def _suffix(filename: str) -> str:
    from pathlib import PurePath

    return PurePath(str(filename or "")).suffix.lower()[:12]


def _internal_schema(tool, apps) -> dict:
    for item in apps:
        if item.manifest.slug != tool.app_slug:
            continue
        for spec in item.manifest.tools:
            if spec.job_type == tool.job_type and (
                    spec.name == tool.name
                    or (spec.api_contract or {}).get("public_name") == tool.name):
                return dict(spec.params_schema)
    raise invalid_request("This tool is no longer available.")


def price(tool, params: dict) -> int:
    """What this call costs, from the platform's single pricing source."""
    from platform_core.registry import RegistryError, credit_for

    try:
        return int(credit_for(tool.job_type, params))
    except RegistryError as exc:
        # A tool whose price cannot be resolved must never run: free execution
        # is money leaving the building silently (Q5, and the invariant in
        # `docs/QUYET_DINH_NEN_TANG.md` §2.4).
        raise invalid_request("This tool cannot be priced right now.") from exc


def submit(db, *, principal, tool, params: dict, quote: dict,
           idempotency_key: str):
    """Hold credit and queue the job in one transaction. Caller commits.

    Raises ``credit.ThieuCreditError`` when the balance is short — and because
    the hold and the job insert share this transaction, the caller's rollback
    leaves neither behind.
    """
    from platform_core.job_submit import submit_with_credit
    from platform_core.public_api.sandbox import is_test

    meta = {
        "tool": tool.name,
        "key_id": principal.key_id,
        # The project the key belongs to, so a project-scoped budget can be
        # measured from the ledger without joining back through the key — which
        # would break the moment a key is rotated or revoked (EXT-11).
        "project_id": str(getattr(principal, "project_id", "") or ""),
        # "live" or "test". The worker reads it to decide whether to call a
        # provider, and every listing reads it to keep the two apart (EXT-12).
        "mode": str(getattr(principal, "mode", "live") or "live"),
        "quote_intent": str(quote.get("intent") or ""),
        # Copied from the signed quote rather than looked up again: what matters
        # for reconciliation is the regime in force when the price was promised,
        # not the one in force when the worker happened to run (EXT-15).
        "pricing_version": str(quote.get("pricing_version") or ""),
        "idempotency_key": str(idempotency_key or ""),
        # The correlation id of the request that created this job, so support
        # and the customer's own log page can walk request → job → events →
        # ledger without a new identifier to keep in step (EXT-09).
        "request_id": str(getattr(principal, "request_id", "") or ""),
    }
    job_params = dict(params)
    # Every app handler in this platform reads `owner_id` from its parameters to
    # scope storage keys and to check that a referenced file belongs to the
    # caller. The UI routes pass it; the API must too, and it must come from the
    # verified principal rather than from anything the request said.
    job_params["owner_id"] = principal.user_id
    job_params[API_META_KEY] = meta

    # The quote's intent is also the dedupe key: a retry that somehow reaches
    # `jobs.submit` directly still cannot open a second job for one quote.
    from platform_core.job_submit import dedupe_key_for

    dedupe = dedupe_key_for(tool.job_type, {
        "intent": meta["quote_intent"], "key_id": principal.key_id})

    if is_test(getattr(principal, "mode", "live")):
        # A test key never reaches the ledger. Not "spends little" — cannot
        # spend, which is the property that makes a leaked test key harmless.
        # Everything else about the submission is the live path, including the
        # dedupe key, so a retry behaves here exactly as it will in production.
        from platform_core import jobs as jobq

        return jobq.submit(
            db, user_id=principal.user_id, app_slug=tool.app_slug,
            job_type=tool.job_type, params=job_params, dedupe_key=dedupe,
        )
    # The quote is a promise: hold exactly what it said. Recomputing here would
    # skip the published price bounds and charge past a number the customer was
    # shown (EXT-15).
    return submit_with_credit(
        db, user_id=principal.user_id, app_slug=tool.app_slug,
        job_type=tool.job_type, params=job_params, dedupe_key=dedupe,
        quoted_credit=int(quote.get("credit", 0)),
    )


def api_meta(job) -> dict:
    """The bookkeeping block this module attached, or an empty dict."""
    meta = (job.params or {}).get(API_META_KEY)
    return dict(meta) if isinstance(meta, dict) else {}

"""Lifecycle of developer API keys: issue, verify, list, revoke, rotate.

Threat model this file is written against
-----------------------------------------

*Stolen database dump.* Only ``HMAC-SHA256(pepper, secret)`` is stored and the
pepper lives in the process environment, not in the database. Without it an
attacker cannot even test guesses offline, and with 256 bits of CSPRNG secret
there is nothing to guess anyway.

*Denial of service through the auth path.* Verification is one HMAC — tens of
microseconds. A password-grade KDF here would let any anonymous caller burn a
CPU core per request; that is a worse bug than the one it would prevent, and the
input is random rather than human-chosen so the KDF buys nothing.

*Key enumeration.* An unknown ``key_id`` and a wrong secret take the same path:
the digest is always computed, the comparison is always ``compare_digest``, and
both answer with the same ``None``. Callers upstream must not tell the two apart
in the response either.

*Write amplification.* ``last_used_at`` is bucketed, so a client polling a job
every two seconds does not turn every read into a row update.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import secrets
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

from platform_core.public_api.scopes import normalize_scopes
from platform_core.public_api.tables import (DeveloperApiKey, KEY_PREFIX,
                                             KEY_PREFIX_TEST, DEVKEY_ACTIVE)

# 32 bytes = 256 bits, urlsafe-base64 without padding -> 43 characters.
SECRET_BYTES = 32
KEY_ID_BYTES = 16          # 128 bits: collisions are not a practical concern
SECRET_LENGTH = 43
KEY_ID_LENGTH = 32
MAX_ISSUE_ATTEMPTS = 3

# How stale ``last_used_at`` is allowed to be. Five minutes is enough for
# "is this key still in use?" and turns a per-request write into a rare one.
LAST_USED_BUCKET = timedelta(minutes=5)

MAX_KEYS_PER_USER = 25
MAX_EXPIRY = timedelta(days=365)
MAX_ALLOWED_IPS = 20

PEPPER_ENV = "LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER"
PEPPER_VERSION_ENV = "LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER_VERSION"
# Retired peppers stay readable so a rotation does not invalidate live keys:
# LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER_V1, LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER_V2, ...
RETIRED_PEPPER_PREFIX = "LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER_V"
MIN_PEPPER_LENGTH = 32

_HEX = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")
_SECRET_ALPHABET = frozenset(
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_")


class DeveloperKeyError(Exception):
    """Refusing to issue/verify because of configuration or bad input."""


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def _aware(value: datetime | None) -> datetime | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    return value if value.tzinfo is not None else value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


# ── Pepper handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def current_pepper(env: dict | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """``(version, secret)`` used for new keys. Raises when unconfigured.

    Deliberately no default value: a built-in fallback pepper is the same as no
    pepper at all, and it would ship silently to every installation.
    """
    values = os.environ if env is None else env
    pepper = str(values.get(PEPPER_ENV, "")).strip()
    if len(pepper) < MIN_PEPPER_LENGTH:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(
            f"{PEPPER_ENV} is missing or too short "
            f"(need at least {MIN_PEPPER_LENGTH} characters).")
    try:
        version = int(str(values.get(PEPPER_VERSION_ENV, "1")).strip() or "1")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(f"{PEPPER_VERSION_ENV} must be an integer.") from exc
    if version < 1:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(f"{PEPPER_VERSION_ENV} must be >= 1.")
    return version, pepper


def pepper_for_version(version: int, env: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """Pepper that produced an existing digest, current or retired."""
    values = os.environ if env is None else env
    active_version, active = current_pepper(values)
    if int(version) == active_version:
        return active
    retired = str(values.get(f"{RETIRED_PEPPER_PREFIX}{int(version)}", "")).strip()
    if len(retired) < MIN_PEPPER_LENGTH:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(
            f"No pepper available for version {version}; keys issued with it "
            "cannot be verified until it is restored or the keys are rotated.")
    return retired


def digest_secret(secret: str, pepper: str) -> str:
    return hmac.new(pepper.encode("utf-8"), secret.encode("utf-8"),
                    hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


# ── Token format ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _new_key_id() -> str:
    return secrets.token_hex(KEY_ID_BYTES)


def _new_secret() -> str:
    return secrets.token_urlsafe(SECRET_BYTES)[:SECRET_LENGTH]


def format_token(key_id: str, secret: str, mode: str = "live") -> str:
    prefix = KEY_PREFIX_TEST if str(mode) == "test" else KEY_PREFIX
    return f"{prefix}_{key_id}_{secret}"


def parse_token(token: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """``ltt_sk_<key_id>_<secret>`` → ``(key_id, secret)``; ``None`` if malformed.

    Structural checks only, and no logging: a malformed token is still a
    credential someone typed, so it must not end up in a log line or an error
    message.
    """
    if not token or not isinstance(token, str):
        return None
    # `maxsplit=3` matters: the secret is urlsafe base64, so it legitimately
    # contains "_" and a plain split() would shred a perfectly valid token.
    parts = token.split("_", 3)
    if len(parts) != 4:                       # "ltt", "sk", key_id, secret
        return None
    if f"{parts[0]}_{parts[1]}" not in (KEY_PREFIX, KEY_PREFIX_TEST):
        return None
    key_id, secret = parts[2], parts[3]
    if len(key_id) != KEY_ID_LENGTH or len(secret) != SECRET_LENGTH:
        return None
    if not all(char in _HEX for char in key_id):
        return None
    if not all(char in _SECRET_ALPHABET for char in secret):
        return None
    return key_id, secret


# ── Issue ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def normalize_ips(values) -> list:
    """Validate an IP allowlist into canonical CIDR strings.

    A bare address is accepted and stored as a /32 (or /128): people think in
    addresses, and silently widening `203.0.113.4` to a range would be the
    opposite of what they asked for.
    """
    import ipaddress

    out: list = []
    for value in values or ():
        raw = str(value).strip()
        if not raw:
            continue
        try:
            network = ipaddress.ip_network(raw, strict=False)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise DeveloperKeyError(
                f"{raw!r} is not an IP address or CIDR block.") from exc
        text = str(network)
        if text not in out:
            out.append(text)
    if len(out) > MAX_ALLOWED_IPS:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(
            f"An API key may list at most {MAX_ALLOWED_IPS} IP ranges.")
    return out


def ip_allowed(key: DeveloperApiKey, address: str) -> bool:
    """Is this key allowed to be presented from ``address``?

    An empty allowlist means anywhere. A non-empty one with an unparseable or
    unknown caller address means **no** — a restriction that silently stops
    applying when the address cannot be determined is not a restriction.
    """
    import ipaddress

    allowed = list(key.allowed_ips or ())
    if not allowed:
        return True
    try:
        caller = ipaddress.ip_address(str(address or "").strip())
    except ValueError:
        return False
    for entry in allowed:
        try:
            if caller in ipaddress.ip_network(str(entry), strict=False):
                return True
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return False


def issue(db, *, user_id: str, name: str = "", scopes=(), allowed_tools=(),
          allowed_ips=(), project_id: str = "", mode: str = "live",
          expires_at: datetime | None = None, env: dict | None = None,
          now: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[DeveloperApiKey, str]:
    """Create a key. Returns the row and the plaintext token **once**.

    The caller must show the plaintext to its owner and then forget it: nothing
    in this module can recover it afterwards, by design.
    """
    current = now or _now()
    version, pepper = current_pepper(env)
    owner = str(user_id or "").strip()
    if not owner:
        raise DeveloperKeyError("A developer key must belong to a user.")

    live = db.execute(select(DeveloperApiKey).where(
        DeveloperApiKey.user_id == owner,
        DeveloperApiKey.revoked_at.is_(None))).scalars().all()
    if len([key for key in live if key.is_usable(now=current)]) >= MAX_KEYS_PER_USER:
        raise DeveloperKeyError(
            f"This account already has {MAX_KEYS_PER_USER} active API keys.")

    expiry = _aware(expires_at)
    if expiry is not None:
        if expiry <= current:
            raise DeveloperKeyError("expires_at must be in the future.")
        if expiry > current + MAX_EXPIRY:
            raise DeveloperKeyError("expires_at must be within one year.")

    clean_scopes = normalize_scopes(scopes)
    clean_tools = _normalize_tools(allowed_tools)
    clean_ips = normalize_ips(allowed_ips)

    # A 128-bit key_id will not collide in practice; retrying anyway means a
    # freak collision (or a truncated generator in a future edit) fails one
    # request instead of raising an opaque IntegrityError at commit time.
    last_error: Exception | None = None
    for _attempt in range(MAX_ISSUE_ATTEMPTS):
        key_id, secret = _new_key_id(), _new_secret()
        key = DeveloperApiKey(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()), user_id=owner, name=str(name or "")[:120],
            key_id=key_id, verifier_digest=digest_secret(secret, pepper),
            pepper_version=version, scopes=clean_scopes,
            allowed_tools=clean_tools, allowed_ips=clean_ips,
            project_id=str(project_id) or None, mode=str(mode or "live"),
            enabled=True, created_at=current, expires_at=expiry,
        )
        db.add(key)
        try:
            db.flush()
        except IntegrityError as exc:
            db.rollback()
            last_error = exc
            continue
        return key, format_token(key_id, secret, key.mode)
    raise DeveloperKeyError("Could not allocate a unique key id.") from last_error


def _normalize_tools(tools) -> list:
    seen, out = set(), []
    for tool in tools or ():
        name = str(tool).strip()
        if name and name not in seen:
            seen.add(name)
            out.append(name)
    return out


# ── Verify ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def verify(db, token: str, *, env: dict | None = None,
           now: datetime | None = None) -> DeveloperApiKey | None:
    """Resolve a bearer token to a usable key, or ``None``.

    Every failure mode returns the same ``None`` and walks the same code path.
    A caller that answered "unknown key" differently from "wrong secret" would
    turn this into an oracle for enumerating valid key ids.
    """
    current = now or _now()
    parsed = parse_token(token)
    if parsed is None:
        _equalize_work(env)
        return None
    key_id, secret = parsed

    key = db.execute(select(DeveloperApiKey).where(
        DeveloperApiKey.key_id == key_id)).scalar_one_or_none()
    if key is None:
        _equalize_work(env)
        return None

    try:
        pepper = pepper_for_version(int(key.pepper_version or 1), env)
    except DeveloperKeyError:
        # A key whose pepper is gone cannot be verified. Failing closed is the
        # only safe answer; the operator sees it as "key stopped working", which
        # is exactly what a missing pepper means.
        return None

    candidate = digest_secret(secret, pepper)
    if not hmac.compare_digest(candidate, str(key.verifier_digest or "")):
        return None
    if not key.is_usable(now=current):
        return None
    return key


def _equalize_work(env: dict | None) -> None:
    """Do the same HMAC for a malformed/unknown token as for a real one."""
    try:
        _version, pepper = current_pepper(env)
    except DeveloperKeyError:
        pepper = "unconfigured-pepper-placeholder-value-only"
    digest_secret(secrets.token_urlsafe(SECRET_BYTES)[:SECRET_LENGTH], pepper)


def touch_last_used(db, key: DeveloperApiKey, *, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    """Refresh ``last_used_at`` at most once per bucket. True when it wrote."""
    current = now or _now()
    previous = _aware(key.last_used_at)
    if previous is not None and current - previous < LAST_USED_BUCKET:
        return False
    key.last_used_at = current
    db.flush()
    return True


# ── Management ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def list_for_user(db, user_id: str) -> list:
    """Metadata for one owner. Never returns anything secret."""
    return list(db.execute(select(DeveloperApiKey).where(
        DeveloperApiKey.user_id == str(user_id or ""),
    ).order_by(DeveloperApiKey.created_at.desc())).scalars().all())


def get_owned(db, *, user_id: str, key_id: str) -> DeveloperApiKey | None:
    """Owner-scoped lookup. The owner filter is in the query, not in an ``if``.

    Fetch-then-check is how object-level authorization gets forgotten; making
    ownership part of the WHERE clause means a miss is indistinguishable from a
    key that does not exist, which is also the right answer to return.
    """
    return db.execute(select(DeveloperApiKey).where(
        DeveloperApiKey.user_id == str(user_id or ""),
        DeveloperApiKey.key_id == str(key_id or ""),
    )).scalar_one_or_none()


def revoke(db, key: DeveloperApiKey, *, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    """Irreversible. Returns False when the key was already revoked."""
    if key.revoked_at is not None:
        return False
    key.revoked_at = now or _now()
    key.enabled = False
    db.flush()
    return True


def set_enabled(db, key: DeveloperApiKey, enabled: bool) -> None:
    """Temporary pause, unlike :func:`revoke` which cannot be undone."""
    if key.revoked_at is not None:
        raise DeveloperKeyError("A revoked key cannot be re-enabled.")
    key.enabled = bool(enabled)
    db.flush()


def rotate(db, key: DeveloperApiKey, *, env: dict | None = None,
           now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """Give an existing key new secret material; the old token stops working.

    In-place rather than issue-and-revoke so scopes, name and history stay on
    one row. For a zero-downtime swap, issue a second key, migrate the client,
    then revoke the first — that is a deployment choice, not a default.
    """
    if key.revoked_at is not None:
        raise DeveloperKeyError("A revoked key cannot be rotated.")
    current = now or _now()
    version, pepper = current_pepper(env)
    for _attempt in range(MAX_ISSUE_ATTEMPTS):
        key_id, secret = _new_key_id(), _new_secret()
        key.key_id = key_id
        key.verifier_digest = digest_secret(secret, pepper)
        key.pepper_version = version
        key.rotated_at = current
        try:
            db.flush()
        except IntegrityError:
            db.rollback()
            continue
        # Same mode as before: rotation replaces secret material, and a key that
        # silently changed world on rotation would point a live integration at
        # mocks (or a test one at the ledger).
        return format_token(key_id, secret, key.mode)
    raise DeveloperKeyError("Could not allocate a unique key id.")


def status_of(key: DeveloperApiKey, *, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    return key.status(now=now)


__all__ = ["DEVKEY_ACTIVE", "DeveloperKeyError", "current_pepper", "digest_secret",
           "format_token", "get_owned", "issue", "list_for_user", "parse_token",
           "pepper_for_version", "revoke", "rotate", "set_enabled", "status_of",
           "touch_last_used", "verify"]
