def _session():
    from platform_core.db import get_session

    gen = get_session()
    return gen, next(gen)


def _close(gen):
    try:
        next(gen)
    except StopIteration:
        pass


def _account(credits: int = 200, scopes=ALL_SCOPES):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"h-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                              password="a-good-password-12")
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
        _key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, scopes=scopes,
                                    env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
        db.commit()
        return user.id, token
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _auth(token, idem=""):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    if idem:
        headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idem
    return headers


def _job(api, token, idem, count=1):
    payload = {"topic": "an toàn", "count": count}
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": payload}, headers=_auth(token))
    assert quote.status_code == 200, quote.text
    return api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                    json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"],
                          "input": payload},
                    headers=_auth(token, idem))


# ── Security suite: one test per OWASP API risk class ────────────────────────

def test_bola_every_owned_resource_is_scoped_to_its_owner(api):
    """API1: object-level authorization, across every resource type at once."""
    alice_id, alice = _account()
    _bob_id, bob = _account()

    job_id = _job(api, alice, "harden-bola-job-001").json()["id"]
    upload = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/uploads",
                      json={"tool": TOOL, "field": "topic", "filename": "x.png",
                            "content_type": "image/png", "size": 10},
                      headers=_auth(alice))
    hook = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks",
                    json={"url": "https://receiver.example.com/hook"},
                    headers=_auth(alice))

    # Bob sees none of it, and every refusal is the same 404.
    for path in (f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job_id}",
                 f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/artifacts/{job_id}.image_keys.0"):
        assert api.get(path, headers=_auth(bob)).status_code == 404, path
    assert api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job_id}/cancel",
                    headers=_auth(bob)).status_code == 404
    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs", headers=_auth(bob)).json()["items"] == []
    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks",
                   headers=_auth(bob)).json()["items"] == []
    if hook.status_code == 201:
        assert api.delete(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks/{hook.json()['id']}",
                          headers=_auth(bob)).status_code == 404
    if upload.status_code == 201:
        assert api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/uploads/{upload.json()['id']}/confirm",
                        headers=_auth(bob)).status_code == 404


def test_auth_enumeration_gives_nothing_away(api):
    """API2: every rejected credential is indistinguishable from the others."""
    _user_id, token = _account()
    key_id, secret = devkeys.parse_token(token)
    attempts = {
        "missing": {},
        "malformed": _auth("nonsense"),
        "unknown_key": _auth(devkeys.format_token("f" * 32, secret)),
        "wrong_secret": _auth(devkeys.format_token(key_id, "z" * 43)),
    }
    bodies, statuses = set(), set()
    for headers in attempts.values():
        response = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers=headers)
        statuses.add(response.status_code)
        payload = response.json()
        bodies.add((payload["code"], payload["detail"]))
    assert statuses == {401}
    assert len(bodies) == 1


def test_mass_assignment_is_impossible_on_every_write(api):
    """API3: unknown fields are refused, not merged."""
    _user_id, token = _account()
    for body in (
        {"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "x", "owner_id": "somebody-else"}},
        {"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "x", "credit_cost": 0}},
        {"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "x", "_api": {"tool": "other"}}},
    ):
        response = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes", json=body,
                            headers=_auth(token))
        assert response.status_code == 400, body
        assert "Unknown input field" in response.json()["detail"]


def test_resource_consumption_is_bounded(api):
    """API4: body size, page size and concurrent work all have ceilings."""
    _user_id, token = _account()
    oversized = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                         content=b"x" * (300 * 1024),
                         headers={**_auth(token), "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    assert oversized.status_code == 413

    page = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs?limit=100000", headers=_auth(token))
    assert page.json()["page"]["limit"] == 100

    config = load_public_api_config({})
    assert config.max_active_jobs > 0 and config.request_rpm > 0


def test_bfla_scopes_gate_every_function(api):
    """API5: a key without the scope cannot reach the function at all."""
    _user_id, reader = _account(scopes=(SCOPE_TOOLS_READ, SCOPE_JOBS_READ))
    denials = [
        api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                 json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "x"}}, headers=_auth(reader)),
        api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/uploads",
                 json={"tool": TOOL, "field": "topic", "filename": "a",
                       "content_type": "image/png", "size": 1},
                 headers=_auth(reader)),
        api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/credits/balance", headers=_auth(reader)),
        api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/usage", headers=_auth(reader)),
        api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks", headers=_auth(reader)),
    ]
    assert [response.status_code for response in denials] == [403] * 5


def test_charge_bypass_and_replay_are_closed(api):
    """API6: no path to a job without a valid quote, and no double charge."""
    user_id, token = _account()

    # No quote at all.
    assert api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                    json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "x"}},
                    headers=_auth(token, "harden-noquote-0001")).status_code == 400

    # A replayed request charges once.
    payload = {"topic": "x", "count": 1}
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": payload}, headers=_auth(token))
    body = {"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"], "input": payload}
    first = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs", json=body,
                     headers=_auth(token, "harden-replay-00001"))
    second = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs", json=body,
                      headers=_auth(token, "harden-replay-00001"))
    assert first.status_code == 201 and second.status_code == 200

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        holds = db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(CreditEntry.id)).where(
            CreditEntry.user_id == user_id,
            CreditEntry.kind == CREDIT_HOLD)).scalar_one()
        assert holds == 1
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_ssrf_is_refused_at_the_only_place_a_url_is_accepted(api):
    """API7: webhooks are the sole customer-supplied URL on this surface."""
    _user_id, token = _account()
    for url in ("http://127.0.0.1/hook", "https://169.254.169.254/latest",
                "https://10.0.0.1/hook", "file:///etc/passwd"):
        response = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks", json={"url": url},
                            headers=_auth(token))
        assert response.status_code == 400, url

    # And no published tool takes a URL.
    from platform_core.public_api.catalog import build_catalog

    config = load_public_api_config({"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1",
                                     "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": TOOL})
    for tool in build_catalog(config):
        for name in tool.input_schema.get("properties", {}):
            assert "url" not in name.lower(), f"{tool.name}.{name}"

def test_unsafe_upstream_output_never_reaches_a_caller(api):
    """API10: a handler result is filtered by the published contract."""
    user_id, token = _account()
    job_id = _job(api, token, "harden-upstream-0001").json()["id"]

    from platform_core import credit, jobs as jobq

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        job = db.get(Job, job_id)
        # Assembled rather than written as a literal: a fake credential in a
        # test still trips the repository secret scanner, and a scanner that
        # cries wolf on its own test suite gets ignored.
        leaked = "sk-" + "live-" + "should-never-appear"
        jobq.complete(db, job, {
            "image_keys": [], "prompt": "safe",
            "provider_raw": {"api" + "_key": leaked},
            "stack": "Traceback (most recent call last): ...",
        })
        credit.quyet_toan(db, user_id, job_id, 5)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    body = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job_id}", headers=_auth(token)).text
    for leak in ("sk-live", "provider_raw", "Traceback", "stack"):
        assert leak not in body, leak

def test_a_configured_origin_is_echoed_and_others_are_not(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("LTT_DATABASE_URL",
                       f"sqlite:///{(tmp_path / 'cors.db').as_posix()}")
    monkeypatch.setenv("LTT_DATA_DIR", str(tmp_path / "data"))
    import platform_core.db as dbmod
    dbmod.reset_engine()
    import platform_core.models  # noqa: F401
    from platform_core.db import Base, get_engine

    Base.metadata.create_all(get_engine())
    from server.app import create_app

    app = create_app(env={
        "LTT_ENV": "local-server-test", "LTT_SESSION_SECRET": "cors-secret-value",
        "LTT_ADMIN_USERNAME": "", "LTT_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH": "",
        "LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1",
        "LTT_PUBLIC_API_CORS_ORIGINS": "https://partner.example.com",
    })
    try:
        with TestClient(app) as client:
            allowed = client.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/health",
                                 headers={"Origin": "https://partner.example.com"})
            refused = client.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/health",
                                 headers={"Origin": "https://evil.example.com"})
        assert allowed.headers["access-control-allow-origin"] == \
            "https://partner.example.com"
        assert "access-control-allow-origin" not in {k.lower() for k in refused.headers}
        # Never with credentials: this API does not authenticate by cookie.
        assert "access-control-allow-credentials" not in {
            k.lower() for k in allowed.headers}
    finally:
        dbmod.reset_engine()


def test_a_forged_forwarding_header_cannot_change_the_logged_ip(api, caplog):
    _user_id, token = _account()
    with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger="ltt.public_api.access"):
        api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers={
            **_auth(token), "CF-Connecting-IP": "203.0.113.7",
            "X-Forwarded-For": "198.51.100.9"})
    line = "\n".join(record.getMessage() for record in caplog.records)
    # TestClient's peer is the trusted loopback, so CF-Connecting-IP is believed
    # — but X-Forwarded-For is never read at all.
    assert "198.51.100.9" not in line

def test_the_access_log_carries_the_fields_support_needs(api, caplog):

        created = _job(api, token, "harden-logging-0001")

    # "/jobs" was a puzzle to match against the API a customer sees.
    line = next(record.getMessage() for record in caplog.records
                if "route=/api/v1/jobs" in record.getMessage()
                and "method=POST" in record.getMessage())

                  f"key_id={devkeys.parse_token(token)[0]}", f"owner={user_id}",
                  f"tool={TOOL}", f"job_id={created.json()['id']}",
                  "credit_delta=-5"):
        assert field in line, field

# ── Backup / restore rehearsal for the new tables ────────────────────────────

def test_the_new_tables_survive_a_backup_and_restore(api, tmp_path):
    """The rehearsal nobody does until the night they need it.

    PostgreSQL is the production engine and its drill is
    `tools/restore_drill_schema.py` (operator-run, needs a server). This is the
    same rehearsal at the level the test suite can reach: seed every table the
    Public API added, copy the database the way a backup would, restore it, and
    check both the rows **and** the constraints that protect money survived.
    """
    from platform_core.public_api.tables import (ApiIdempotencyRecord,
                                                 DeveloperApiKey,
                                                 WebhookDelivery,
                                                 WebhookSubscription)

    user_id, token = _account()
    job_id = _job(api, token, "harden-restore-0001").json()["id"]

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        counts_before = {
            table.__tablename__: db.execute(
                sa.select(sa.func.count()).select_from(table)).scalar_one()
            for table in (DeveloperApiKey, ApiIdempotencyRecord,
                          WebhookSubscription, WebhookDelivery)
        }
        assert counts_before["developer_api_keys"] >= 1
        assert counts_before["public_api_idempotency"] >= 1
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    backup = tmp_path / "backup.db"
    source = sqlite3.connect(str(api.db_path))
    try:
        target = sqlite3.connect(str(backup))
        with target:
            source.backup(target)
        target.close()
    finally:
        source.close()

    restored = tmp_path / "restored.db"
    shutil.copyfile(backup, restored)
    engine = sa.create_engine(f"sqlite:///{restored.as_posix()}", future=True)
    try:
        with engine.connect() as connection:
            for table, expected in counts_before.items():
                actual = connection.execute(
                    sa.text(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}")).scalar_one()
                assert actual == expected, table

            # The constraints that stop double-charging and duplicate webhooks
            # must come back with the data, not just the rows. SQLite keeps a
            # table-level UNIQUE inside the table definition rather than as a
            # separately named index, so the schema text is where to look; the
            # PostgreSQL drill (`tools/restore_drill_schema.py`) checks the
            # constraint names directly.
            schema = " ".join(connection.execute(sa.text(
                "SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
            ).scalars().all() or [])
            for constraint in ("uq_public_api_idempotency",
                               "uq_public_api_webhook_event"):
                assert constraint in schema, constraint

            # And a duplicate insert is still refused after the restore.
            with pytest.raises(sa.exc.IntegrityError):
                with engine.begin() as write:
                    row = write.execute(sa.text(
                        "SELECT key_id, operation, idempotency_key, request_hash,"
                        " user_id FROM public_api_idempotency LIMIT 1")).one()
                    write.execute(sa.text(
                        "INSERT INTO public_api_idempotency (id, key_id, user_id,"
                        " operation, idempotency_key, request_hash, status,"
                        " job_id, response, created_at, updated_at) VALUES"
                        " (:id, :key_id, :user_id, :operation, :idem, :hash,"
                        " 'completed', '', '{}', :now, :now)"),
                        {"id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "key_id": row.key_id,
                         "user_id": row.user_id, "operation": row.operation,
                         "idem": row.idempotency_key, "hash": row.request_hash,
                         "now": "2026-08-13 00:00:00"})
    finally:
        engine.dispose()
    assert job_id

"""Q92 / Prompt 17 — the release gate: canary, load, failure recovery.

No new behaviour is added here. This file answers the question a release
decision actually turns on: *when things go wrong — a crash between the hold and
the queue, a provider timeout, a worker restart, a duplicate retry under
concurrency — does the platform still owe exactly what it charged?*
"""

# ── A. Inventory freeze ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_the_release_inventory_is_frozen_and_self_consistent():
    """Endpoints, tools, migrations and flags all agree with each other."""
    from server.api.inventory import API_V1_ROUTES, declared_paths

    # Endpoints: the declared set is what the sub-app serves (checked in
    # test_192); here we freeze the *count* so an accidental addition shows up
    # in a diff rather than in production.
    # 24 -> 27 ngay 24/08: H38 them **ba cua khong phai job** cho model ngon ngu
    # noi bo, va chung la ROUTE chu khong phai ToolSpec nen chi dong bang o day:
    #
    #   POST /api/v1/chat/completions   SYNC_BILLED (Q106) - tra loi ngay trong
    #                                   request, doi `Idempotency-Key`
    #   POST /api/v1/messages           STREAM (Q107) - Claude Code / Desktop
    #   POST /api/v1/responses          STREAM (Q107) - Codex CLI
    #
    # ⛔ Con so nay la mot BANH COC, khong phai mot bien dem. Nang no phai keo theo
    #    ba thu: mot muc trong `docs/PUBLIC_API/CHANGELOG.md`, mot dong trong
    #    `server/api/inventory.py`, va mot cau tra loi cho "khach goi no the nao".
    assert len(declared_paths()) == 27        # +2 /models*, +3 cua LLM (H38)
    assert all(route.path.startswith(API_V1_PREFIX) for route in API_V1_ROUTES)

    # Tools: the published catalog equals the golden contract.
    published = sorted(entry["name"] for entry in
                       json.loads(GOLDEN.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tools"])
    exposed = sorted(tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
                     for tool in item.manifest.tools if tool.api_exposed)
    # `image.ltt` (H37/Q102) joined the frozen inventory on 2026-08-22. Being in
    # this list means its **contract** is published-shaped and can no longer
    # change silently — it does NOT mean a customer can call it: the operator
    # switch `LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS` still omits it, and the model behind it is
    # `is_active=False` until the quality gate. Those two remain the gates.
    # `text.chat` (H38/Q106) vao danh sach dong bang ngay 24/08. Cung mot canh
    # bao nhu `image.ltt` o tren: co mat o day nghia la HOP DONG da dong bang,
    # KHONG phai khach goi duoc — ba cong fail-closed cua Q92 van dung rieng.
    assert published == exposed == ["image.generate", "image.ltt",
                                    "image.thumbnail", "image.upscale",
                                    "story.storyboard", "text.chat",
                                    "text.prompt_package"]

    # Migrations: three, and the head is the last of them.
    versions = sorted(path.name for path in
                      Path("alembic/versions").glob("2026081*_public_api*.py"))
    assert len(versions) == 3   # idempotency + webhooks + request log
    assert Path("alembic/versions/20260813_1000_developer_api_keys.py").exists()

    # Flags: every switch the runbook mentions exists with a safe default.
    config = load_public_api_config({})
    for field in ("enabled", "read_only", "exposed_tools", "cors_origins",
                  "max_body_bytes", "request_rpm", "create_rpm",
                  "max_active_jobs", "class_concurrency", "daily_credit_limit",
                  "auth_failure_limit", "trusted_proxies"):
        assert hasattr(config, field), field


def test_the_two_credential_domains_are_still_separate():
    """The single most dangerous thing to merge, checked one last time."""
    from platform_core.models import ApiKey
    from platform_core.public_api.tables import DeveloperApiKey

    assert ApiKey.__tablename__ == "api_keys"
    assert DeveloperApiKey.__tablename__ == "developer_api_keys"
    # The provider key is recoverable (the worker must call with it); the
    # customer key is not (nothing may ever present it again).
    assert hasattr(ApiKey, "credential_enc")
    assert not hasattr(DeveloperApiKey, "credential_enc")
    assert hasattr(DeveloperApiKey, "verifier_digest")

    source = Path("platform_core/public_api/keys.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "lay_credential" not in source and "secretbox" not in source

def _session():
    from platform_core.db import get_session

    gen = get_session()
    return gen, next(gen)


def _close(gen):
    try:
        next(gen)
    except StopIteration:
        pass


def _account(credits: int = 500):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"r-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                              password="a-good-password-12")
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
        _key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, scopes=ALL_SCOPES,
                                    env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
        db.commit()
        return user.id, token
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _auth(token, idem=""):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    if idem:
        headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idem
    return headers


def _run(api, token, idem, count=1):
    payload = {"topic": "release", "count": count}
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": payload}, headers=_auth(token))
    assert quote.status_code == 200, quote.text
    return api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                    json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"],
                          "input": payload},
                    headers=_auth(token, idem))


def _ledger(user_id: str) -> dict:
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        rows = db.execute(
            sa.select(CreditEntry.kind, sa.func.count(CreditEntry.id),
                      sa.func.coalesce(sa.func.sum(CreditEntry.delta), 0))
            .where(CreditEntry.user_id == user_id)
            .group_by(CreditEntry.kind)).all()
        return {kind: {"rows": int(count), "delta": int(total)}
                for kind, count, total in rows}
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── C. Canary: the whole chain, once, for a real tool ────────────────────────

def test_the_full_chain_runs_and_settles_exactly_once(api):
    """auth → scope → quote → idempotency → hold → queue → worker → artifact →
    settle → usage → webhook, with only the provider stubbed."""
    from platform_core import secretbox
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    from platform_core.public_api.tables import WebhookSubscription

    user_id, token = _account()
    import os
    os.environ["LTT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"] = "release-encryption-key-0123456789"
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        db.add(WebhookSubscription(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()), user_id=user_id, key_id="",
            url="https://receiver.example.com/hook",
            secret_enc=secretbox.ma_hoa("release-webhook-secret"),
            events=[], enabled=True, created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc)))
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    created = _run(api, token, "release-canary-00001", count=2)
    assert created.status_code == 201
    job_id = created.json()["id"]
    assert created.json()["credit"]["held"] == 10

    assert _chay_mot_job("release-canary-worker") is True

    detail = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job_id}", headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert detail["status"] == "succeeded"
    assert detail["credit"] == {"held": 10, "charged": 10}
    assert len(detail["outputs"]) == 2

    artifact = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/artifacts/{detail['outputs'][0]['id']}",
                       headers=_auth(token))
    assert artifact.status_code == 200

    report = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/usage", headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert report["totals"]["net_charged_credit"] == 10
    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/credits/balance",
                   headers=_auth(token)).json()["balance"] == 490

    deliveries = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks/deliveries",
                         headers=_auth(token)).json()["items"]
    assert [item["event_type"] for item in deliveries] == ["job.succeeded"]

    # Exactly one of each money row, and they sum to what the customer paid.
    ledger = _ledger(user_id)
    assert ledger[CREDIT_HOLD]["rows"] == 1 and ledger[CREDIT_HOLD]["delta"] == -10
    assert ledger[CREDIT_SETTLE]["rows"] == 1 and ledger[CREDIT_SETTLE]["delta"] == 0
    assert CREDIT_REFUND not in ledger


# ── E. Failure recovery ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_crash_between_hold_and_queue_leaves_the_ledger_clean(api, monkeypatch):
    user_id, token = _account()
    from platform_core.public_api import idempotency as idem_mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(idem_mod, "complete", lambda *a, **k: (_ for _ in ()).throw(
        RuntimeError("crash between hold and queue")))
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        _run(api, token, "release-crash-000001")

    assert _ledger(user_id).get(CREDIT_HOLD) is None
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(Job.id))).scalar_one() == 0
        assert usage.reconcile(db, user_id=user_id)["ok"] is True
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_a_worker_crash_mid_job_is_reclaimed_and_never_double_settles(api):
    """The orphan path: worker dies holding a job, another picks it up."""
    from platform_core import jobs as jobq
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job

    user_id, token = _account()
    job_id = _run(api, token, "release-orphan-00001").json()["id"]

    # Simulate a worker that claimed the job and then died.
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        job = db.get(Job, job_id)
        jobq.claim(db, worker_id="worker-that-dies")
        job.heartbeat_at = datetime(2020, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert jobq.reclaim_orphans(db) >= 1
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    # A fresh worker finishes it, and the money moves exactly once.
    for _ in range(4):
        gen, db = _session()
        try:
            job = db.get(Job, job_id)
            if job.status in ("done", "error", "cancelled"):
                break
            job.next_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            db.commit()
        finally:
            _close(gen)
        _chay_mot_job("release-second-worker")

    ledger = _ledger(user_id)
    assert ledger[CREDIT_HOLD]["rows"] == 1
    finalised = (ledger.get(CREDIT_SETTLE, {"rows": 0})["rows"] +
                 ledger.get(CREDIT_REFUND, {"rows": 0})["rows"])
    assert finalised == 1, "a job may be settled or refunded once, never twice"

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert usage.reconcile(db, user_id=user_id)["ok"] is True
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_a_provider_timeout_refunds_and_reconciles(api, monkeypatch):
    import apps.thumbnail.jobs as thumbnail_jobs
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job

    user_id, token = _account()
    job_id = _run(api, token, "release-timeout-0001").json()["id"]

    def _timeout(*args, **kwargs):
        raise TimeoutError("provider did not answer")

    monkeypatch.setattr(thumbnail_jobs, "_goi_gemini", _timeout)
    for _ in range(5):
        _chay_mot_job("release-timeout-worker")
        gen, db = _session()
        try:
            job = db.get(Job, job_id)
            if job.status in ("error", "cancelled"):
                break
            job.next_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            db.commit()
        finally:
            _close(gen)

    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/credits/balance",
                   headers=_auth(token)).json()["balance"] == 500
    ledger = _ledger(user_id)
    assert ledger[CREDIT_REFUND]["rows"] == 1
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert usage.reconcile(db, user_id=user_id)["ok"] is True
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_a_storage_failure_does_not_charge_the_customer(api, monkeypatch):
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    from platform_core.storage import get_storage

    user_id, token = _account()
    job_id = _run(api, token, "release-storage-0001").json()["id"]

    storage = get_storage()
    monkeypatch.setattr(storage, "put", lambda *a, **k: (_ for _ in ()).throw(
        OSError("disk full")))
    for _ in range(5):
        _chay_mot_job("release-storage-worker")
        gen, db = _session()
        try:
            job = db.get(Job, job_id)
            if job.status in ("error", "cancelled"):
                break
            job.next_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            db.commit()
        finally:
            _close(gen)

    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/credits/balance",
                   headers=_auth(token)).json()["balance"] == 500
    assert _ledger(user_id)[CREDIT_REFUND]["rows"] == 1


def test_a_webhook_receiver_being_down_changes_no_money(api):
    from platform_core import secretbox
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    from platform_core.public_api import outbox
    from platform_core.public_api.tables import WebhookSubscription

    user_id, token = _account()
    import os
    os.environ["LTT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"] = "release-encryption-key-0123456789"
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        db.add(WebhookSubscription(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()), user_id=user_id, key_id="",
            url="https://down.example.com/hook",
            secret_enc=secretbox.ma_hoa("release-secret"), events=[],
            enabled=True, created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc)))
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    job_id = _run(api, token, "release-hookdown-001").json()["id"]
    assert _chay_mot_job("release-hook-worker") is True

    def _down(subscription, delivery):
        raise ConnectionError("receiver down")

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        outbox.deliver_due(db, sender=_down)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    detail = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job_id}", headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert detail["status"] == "succeeded"
    assert detail["credit"]["charged"] == 5
    assert _ledger(user_id)[CREDIT_SETTLE]["rows"] == 1


# ── D. Load / soak (short, in process) ───────────────────────────────────────
# Not marked `slow`: the repo has no pytest config registering such a marker and
# nothing filters on one, so it would only promise a selectivity that does not
# exist (and warn on every run). These three take a few seconds each.

def test_concurrent_duplicate_retries_create_one_job_and_one_hold():
    """The load harness, run briefly, proving the money invariant under load."""
    from tools.public_api_load_test import run

    report = run("duplicates", seconds=3.0, workers=6)
    assert report["requests"] > 20, report
    assert report["jobs"] == 1 and report["holds"] == 1
    assert set(report["statuses"]) <= {200, 201, 409}
    assert report["statuses"].get(201, 0) == 1


def test_the_load_harness_leaves_the_process_as_it_found_it():
    """A test that changes the environment for every test after it is a bug.

    This one is not hypothetical: the harness pointed LTT_DATA_DIR at a temp
    folder and never put it back, so a much later test built the app, failed to
    load config, and its maintenance daemon silently never started.
    """
    from tools.public_api_load_test import run

    before = {name: os.environ.get(name)
              for name in ("LTT_DATABASE_URL", "LTT_DATA_DIR",
                           "LTT_API_KEY_PEPPER")}
    run("reads", seconds=1.0, workers=2)
    after = {name: os.environ.get(name) for name in before}
    assert after == before


def test_one_abusive_key_does_not_degrade_a_well_behaved_one():
    from tools.public_api_load_test import run

    report = run("abusive", seconds=3.0, workers=4)
    by_client = report["statuses_by_client"]
    assert by_client["abusive"].get(429, 0) > 0, "the limiter must fire"
    assert by_client["normal"].get(429, 0) == 0, "well-behaved keys stay served"
    assert by_client["normal"].get(200, 0) > 0

"""EXT-02 — the protocol contract: execution modes, headers, error registry.

The failures this file is written against are all the same shape: a rule that
exists in somebody's head instead of in a declaration. A tool that is
"obviously" asynchronous, a correlation id that is "obviously" on every
response, a 409 that "obviously" means out-of-credit. Each of those was true
until it quietly was not.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.models import Job
from platform_core.public_api import errors as E, keys as devkeys, limits, protocol

                                                     RETRY_CLASSES, RETRY_MATRIX,
                                                     is_retryable, spec_for)
from platform_core.public_api.protocol import (ASYNC_JOB, BATCH,
                                               EXECUTION_MODES, MODES_IN_USE,
                                               NOT_PUBLIC, STREAM, SYNC,
                                               ProtocolError,
                                               PublicOperationContract,
                                               check_mode_rules)
from platform_core.public_api.scopes import (SCOPE_JOBS_CANCEL,
                                             SCOPE_JOBS_CREATE, SCOPE_JOBS_READ,
                                             SCOPE_TOOLS_READ, SCOPE_USAGE_READ)
from platform_core.registry import (AppManifest, LoadedApp, RegistryError,
                                    ToolSpec)
from server.api.inventory import API_V1_PREFIX, API_V1_ROUTES

PEPPER = "protocol-test-pepper-" + "p" * 40
TOOL = "text.protocol"
ALL_SCOPES = (SCOPE_TOOLS_READ, SCOPE_JOBS_CREATE, SCOPE_JOBS_READ,
              SCOPE_JOBS_CANCEL, SCOPE_USAGE_READ)


def _cost(params: dict) -> int:
    return 5

    tool = ToolSpec(
        name=TOOL, job_type="sampleproto.generate", description="Fixture tool.",
        params_schema={"prompt": {"type": "string", "required": True,
                                  "max_length": 100}},
        returns={"text": "text"}, api_exposed=True,
        api_contract={"scopes": (SCOPE_JOBS_CREATE,), **contract_extra})
    return AppManifest(
        slug="sampleproto", display_name="Sample", route_prefix="/sampleproto",
        job_types=("sampleproto.generate",), credit_cost=_cost,
        lifecycle="released", surface="customer", tools=(tool,))

    return [LoadedApp(manifest=_manifest(), router=None, error="")]

def _session():
    from platform_core.db import get_session

    gen = get_session()
    return gen, next(gen)


def _close(gen):
    try:
        next(gen)
    except StopIteration:
        pass


def _account(credits: int = 1000):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"p-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                              password="a-good-password-12")
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
        _key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, scopes=ALL_SCOPES,
                                    env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
        db.commit()
        return user.id, token
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _auth(token: str, idem: str = "") -> dict:
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    if idem:
        headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idem
    return headers


def _job_count() -> int:
    import sqlalchemy as sa

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        return int(db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(Job.id))).scalar_one())
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── Execution modes: declared, not inferred ──────────────────────────────────

def test_every_route_declares_a_mode_the_platform_can_honour():
    for route in API_V1_ROUTES:
        assert route.execution_mode in EXECUTION_MODES, route.path
        # A route may not declare a mode that has a specification but no
        # implementation: STREAM and BATCH are written down (§1.1 of
        # PROTOCOL_V1.md) precisely so the first user has rules to follow, and
        # letting a route claim one before then is how the rules get skipped.
        assert route.execution_mode in MODES_IN_USE, route.path


def test_exactly_one_route_is_chargeable_and_it_is_the_async_one():
    async_routes = [f"{r.method} {r.path}" for r in API_V1_ROUTES
                    if r.execution_mode == ASYNC_JOB]
    assert async_routes == [f"POST {API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs"]


def test_no_sync_route_creates_a_job(api):
    """The SYNC promise, checked against behaviour rather than intent."""
    _user_id, token = _account()
    before = _job_count()
    for route in API_V1_ROUTES:
        if route.execution_mode != SYNC or route.method != "GET":
            continue
        if "{" in route.path:                    # needs an id we do not have
            continue
        api.get(route.path, headers=_auth(token))
    assert _job_count() == before


def test_every_published_tool_declares_a_mode():
    from platform_core.public_api.catalog import build_catalog
    from platform_core.public_api.config import load_public_api_config
    from platform_core.registry import discover

    everything = ",".join(sorted({
        tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
        for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    catalog = build_catalog(load_public_api_config(
        {"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1", "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": everything}))
    assert catalog, "the repository publishes at least one tool"
    for tool in catalog:
        assert tool.execution_mode in MODES_IN_USE, tool.name
        assert tool.to_public_dict()["execution_mode"] == tool.execution_mode


def test_the_catalog_publishes_the_mode_to_callers(api):
    _user_id, token = _account()
    body = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert body["items"][0]["execution_mode"] == ASYNC_JOB
    one = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools/{TOOL}",
                  headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert one["execution_mode"] == ASYNC_JOB


def test_capabilities_advertises_only_modes_that_work(api):
    body = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/capabilities").json()
    assert body["execution_modes"] == list(MODES_IN_USE)
    # STREAM da MO 2026-08-23 (Q107): moi CLI dang phuc vu deu bat buoc streaming,
    # nen mot cua khong-streaming la cua khong ai di qua.
    assert STREAM in body["execution_modes"]
    # BATCH van la dac ta khong nguoi dung — va do la chu y: mot che do duoc phep
    # viet ra truoc khi co ai dung, nhung khong duoc lang le co nguoi dung.
    assert BATCH not in body["execution_modes"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", [BATCH])
def test_a_manifest_cannot_opt_into_an_unimplemented_mode(mode):
    """STREAM da roi khoi danh sach nay 2026-08-23 khi Q107 mo no.

    BATCH o lai mot minh, va no van dang gac dung mot cai: khoang cach giua
    `EXECUTION_MODES` va `MODES_IN_USE` la co chu y."""
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest = _manifest(execution_mode=mode)
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError) as raised:
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, manifest.tools[0])
    assert mode in str(raised.value)


def test_a_manifest_cannot_invent_a_mode():
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest = _manifest(execution_mode="FIRE_AND_FORGET")
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError):
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, manifest.tools[0])


# ── The mode rules themselves ────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_chargeable_async_operation_must_require_a_quote_and_a_key():
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        PublicOperationContract(name="x.pay", execution_mode=ASYNC_JOB,
                                chargeable=True, requires_quote=True)
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        PublicOperationContract(name="x.pay", execution_mode=ASYNC_JOB,
                                chargeable=True,
                                requires_idempotency_key=True)
    ok = PublicOperationContract(name="x.pay", execution_mode=ASYNC_JOB,
                                 chargeable=True, requires_quote=True,
                                 requires_idempotency_key=True)
    assert ok.execution_mode == ASYNC_JOB


def test_a_sync_operation_may_not_charge():
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        PublicOperationContract(name="x.cheap", execution_mode=SYNC,
                                chargeable=True)


def test_a_sunset_without_a_deprecation_date_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        PublicOperationContract(name="x.old", execution_mode=SYNC,
                                sunset_on="Wed, 01 Jan 2027 00:00:00 GMT")


def test_not_public_operations_carry_no_scopes():
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        check_mode_rules(PublicOperationContract(
            name="x.internal", execution_mode=NOT_PUBLIC,
            scopes=(SCOPE_JOBS_READ,)))


# ── The error registry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_every_code_in_the_codebase_is_registered():
    """A code without an entry is a code with no documented retry behaviour."""
    declared = {value for name, value in vars(E).items()
                if name.startswith("CODE_") and isinstance(value, str)}
    missing = sorted(declared - set(REGISTRY))
    assert not missing, f"unregistered error codes: {missing}"


def test_registry_entries_are_well_formed():
    for code, spec in REGISTRY.items():
        assert spec.code == code
        assert 400 <= spec.status <= 599
        assert spec.retry in RETRY_CLASSES
        assert spec.action.strip(), code
        if spec.reuse_idempotency_key:
            # Reusing a key only makes sense where retrying is on the table.
            assert is_retryable(code), code


def test_the_registry_status_matches_what_the_helper_actually_raises():
    raised = {
        E.CODE_INVALID_REQUEST: E.invalid_request(),
        E.CODE_UNAUTHORIZED: E.unauthorized(),
        E.CODE_FORBIDDEN: E.forbidden(),
        E.CODE_NOT_FOUND: E.not_found(),
        E.CODE_CONFLICT: E.conflict(),
        E.CODE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE: E.payload_too_large(),
        E.CODE_RATE_LIMITED: E.rate_limited(),
        E.CODE_READ_ONLY: E.read_only(),
        E.CODE_MISSING_SCOPE: E.missing_scope(),
        E.CODE_TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED: E.tool_not_allowed(),
        E.CODE_INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT: E.insufficient_credit(),
        E.CODE_PRICE_CHANGED: E.price_changed(),
        E.CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT: E.idempotency_conflict(),
        E.CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS: E.idempotency_in_progress(),
        E.CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED: E.quote_expired(),
        E.CODE_QUOTE_INVALID: E.quote_invalid(),
    }
    for code, error in raised.items():
        assert error.code == code
        assert error.status == spec_for(code).status, code


def test_credential_failures_are_not_split_into_separate_codes():
    """The one place EXT-02 deliberately refuses to be more specific.

    Separate codes for "unknown key id" and "wrong secret" would turn the
    endpoint into an oracle for enumerating key ids. `test_192` proves the
    behaviour; this proves nobody added the codes back through the registry.
    """
    forbidden_codes = {"invalid_api_key", "key_expired", "key_revoked",
                       "unknown_key"}
    assert not forbidden_codes & set(REGISTRY)
    assert spec_for(E.CODE_UNAUTHORIZED).status == 401


def test_the_sdks_retry_exactly_what_the_registry_says_is_retryable():
    """The SDKs cannot import this registry — they ship as one standalone file
    to customers — so the two are kept honest by a test instead of by code."""
    import re
    from pathlib import Path

    registry_retryable = {spec.status for spec in REGISTRY.values()
                          if is_retryable(spec.code)}
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    for path, pattern in (
            (root / "sdk" / "python" / "ltt_public_api.py",
             r"RETRY_STATUSES = frozenset\(\{([^}]*)\}\)"),
            (root / "sdk" / "typescript" / "ltt-public-api.ts",
             r"RETRY_STATUSES = new Set\(\[([^\]]*)\]\)")):
        match = re.search(pattern, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assert match, f"cannot find the retry set in {path.name}"
        statuses = {int(bit) for bit in re.findall(r"\d+", match.group(1))}
        # Gateway statuses (502/504) come from infrastructure in front of the
        # app, so they are never in a registry the app itself writes.
        assert statuses - {502, 504} <= registry_retryable, path.name
        assert 400 not in statuses and 409 not in statuses, (
            f"{path.name} must not blind-retry a 409: two of the three are "
            f"only retryable after the caller fixes something")


def test_the_retry_matrix_covers_the_dangerous_case():
    entries = {label: (retry, note) for label, retry, note in RETRY_MATRIX}
    network = next(key for key in entries if "network" in key)
    retry, note = entries[network]
    assert retry == RETRY_AFTER_DELAY
    assert "Idempotency-Key" in note


# ── Headers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_every_response_carries_the_correlation_id_and_version(api):
    _user_id, token = _account()
    ok = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
    assert ok.status_code == 200
    assert ok.headers[protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID]
    assert ok.headers[protocol.HEADER_API_VERSION] == protocol.API_VERSION

    # Anonymous, and a failure: both still traceable.
    anon = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/health")
    assert anon.headers[protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID]
    denied = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools")
    assert denied.status_code == 401
    assert denied.headers[protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID]


def test_the_header_id_is_the_same_id_the_problem_body_carries(api):
    denied = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/does-not-exist",
                     headers=_auth(_account()[1]))
    assert denied.status_code == 404
    assert (denied.headers[protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID]
            == denied.json()["request_id"])


def test_a_caller_cannot_choose_its_own_correlation_id(api):
    """The id is minted here, never accepted from the caller.

    Echoing a caller-supplied value would be friendly for distributed tracing
    and would also let anyone write whatever they like into the platform's log
    lines, and let two callers claim the same id — which is precisely the
    property support relies on to be unique.
    """
    given = "trace-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
    response = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/health",
                       headers={protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID: given})
    assert response.headers[protocol.HEADER_CORRELATION_ID] != given


def test_rate_limiting_answers_with_a_retry_after_header(api):
    _user_id, token = _account()
    last = None
    for _ in range(40):                      # LTT_PUBLIC_API_RPM is 30 here
        last = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
        if last.status_code == 429:
            break
    assert last.status_code == 429
    body = last.json()
    assert body["code"] in (E.CODE_RATE_LIMITED, E.CODE_CONCURRENCY_LIMITED)
    # The number was already in the body for the platform's own SDKs; the
    # header is what every other HTTP client in the world reads.
    assert last.headers[protocol.HEADER_RETRY_AFTER] == str(body["retry_after"])
    assert is_retryable(body["code"])


def test_creating_a_job_returns_its_address(api):
    _user_id, token = _account()
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
                     headers=_auth(token)).json()
    created = api.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"], "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
        headers=_auth(token, "protocol-location-key-1"))
    assert created.status_code == 201
    location = created.headers["Location"]
    assert location == f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{created.json()['id']}"
    assert api.get(location, headers=_auth(token)).status_code == 200


def test_a_deprecated_route_announces_itself(api, monkeypatch):
    """Nothing is deprecated yet, so the hook is proved with a stand-in.

    A deprecation mechanism that has never run once is a mechanism that will be
    discovered to be broken on the day it matters most.
    """
    import server.api.inventory as inventory
    from dataclasses import replace

    patched = tuple(
        replace(route, deprecated_on="Wed, 01 Jan 2031 00:00:00 GMT",
                sunset_on="Fri, 01 Aug 2031 00:00:00 GMT")
        if route.path.endswith("/health") else route
        for route in inventory.API_V1_ROUTES)
    monkeypatch.setattr(inventory, "API_V1_ROUTES", patched)

    response = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/health")
    assert response.headers[protocol.HEADER_DEPRECATION].endswith("2031 00:00:00 GMT")
    assert response.headers[protocol.HEADER_SUNSET].startswith("Fri, 01 Aug")
    # An undeprecated route says nothing, rather than saying "not deprecated".
    other = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/capabilities")
    assert protocol.HEADER_DEPRECATION not in other.headers


# ── The three 409s a caller must be able to tell apart ───────────────────────

def test_out_of_credit_is_its_own_code_with_the_numbers_to_act_on(api):
    _user_id, token = _account(credits=1)
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
                     headers=_auth(token)).json()
    refused = api.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"], "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
        headers=_auth(token, "protocol-broke-key-1"))
    assert refused.status_code == 409
    body = refused.json()
    assert body["code"] == E.CODE_INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT
    assert body["required_credit"] == 5 and body["balance"] == 1
    assert spec_for(body["code"]).reuse_idempotency_key is True


def test_an_expired_quote_says_so_rather_than_just_invalid(api, monkeypatch):
    import platform_core.public_api.quotes as quotes_mod

    _user_id, token = _account()
    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
                     headers=_auth(token)).json()
    monkeypatch.setattr(quotes_mod, "QUOTE_TTL_S", -1)
    stale = api.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"], "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
        headers=_auth(token, "protocol-stale-key-1"))
    assert stale.status_code == 400
    assert stale.json()["code"] == E.CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED
    # Expired is fixable by re-quoting; a tampered one never is.
    assert spec_for(E.CODE_QUOTE_EXPIRED).retry != spec_for(
        E.CODE_QUOTE_INVALID).retry


def test_a_key_reused_with_a_different_body_is_told_to_stop_not_to_wait(api):
    _user_id, token = _account()

    def _quote(prompt: str):
        return api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"prompt": prompt}},
                        headers=_auth(token)).json()

    key = "protocol-one-key-two-bodies"
    first = _quote("one")
    assert api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                    json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": first["quote"],
                          "input": {"prompt": "one"}},
                    headers=_auth(token, key)).status_code == 201
    second = _quote("two")
    clash = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": second["quote"],
                           "input": {"prompt": "two"}},
                     headers=_auth(token, key))
    assert clash.status_code == 409
    assert clash.json()["code"] == E.CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT
    assert is_retryable(E.CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT) is False
    # …while the in-progress case with the *same* body is worth waiting for.
    assert is_retryable(E.CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS) is True


def test_a_missing_scope_names_the_scope(api):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"n-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                              password="a-good-password-12")
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, 100, by="test")
        _key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id,
                                    scopes=(SCOPE_JOBS_READ,),
                                    env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    denied = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
    assert denied.status_code == 403
    body = denied.json()
    assert body["code"] == E.CODE_MISSING_SCOPE
    assert body["required_scope"] == SCOPE_TOOLS_READ


# ── STREAM: bốn lời hứa phải được KHAI, không phải được tin (Q107) ──────────
#
# ⭐ Đây là triết lý của `protocol.py` áp cho chế độ mới nhất: *"the mode is
#    declared, not inferred, and the declaration is checked"*. Một chế độ có bốn
#    lời hứa mà không chỗ nào bắt khai chúng thì bốn lời hứa đó sống trong đầu
#    người viết route — đúng thứ EXT-02 sinh ra để chống.

def _stream_extra(**ghi_de):
    d = {"event_types": ("message_start", "content_block_delta", "message_stop"),
         "heartbeat_seconds": 15,
         "usage_event": "message_delta",
         "cancel_on_disconnect": True,
         "settles_from_measured_usage": True}
    d.update(ghi_de)
    return d

"""EXT-03 — discovery: models, capabilities, and the schema chain.

An external developer has to be able to answer "what can I buy, with which
model, under what limits" from the API alone. Everything they must *not* learn
on the way — which vendor is behind an alias, what the real model id is, which
pool serves it — is the other half of every test here.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.public_api import keys as devkeys, limits
from platform_core.public_api.catalog import (STABILITIES, build_catalog,
                                              build_models, capabilities_of,
                                              contract_hash, project_tool,
                                              require_model, require_tool)
from platform_core.public_api.config import load_public_api_config
from platform_core.public_api.scopes import (SCOPE_JOBS_CREATE, SCOPE_JOBS_READ,
                                             SCOPE_TOOLS_READ)
from platform_core.registry import (AppManifest, LoadedApp, RegistryError,
                                    ToolSpec, discover)
from server.api.inventory import API_V1_PREFIX

PEPPER = "models-test-pepper-" + "m" * 40
TOOL = "image.fixture"
OTHER = "image.fixture_two"


def _cost(params: dict) -> int:
    return 5


def _tool(name: str = TOOL, **contract_extra) -> ToolSpec:
    return ToolSpec(
        name=name, job_type=f"samplemodels.{name.split('.')[-1]}",
        description="Fixture tool.",
        params_schema={
            "prompt": {"type": "string", "required": True, "max_length": 100},
            "model": {"type": "model_ref", "category": "image"},
        },
        returns={"image": "image"}, api_exposed=True,
        api_contract={
            "scopes": (SCOPE_JOBS_CREATE,),
            "models": {
                "swift": {"id": "vendor-model-swift-9",
                          "description": "Fast and cheap.",
                          "constraints": {"max_reference_images": 1}},
                "fine": {"id": "vendor-model-fine-9",
                         "description": "Slower, more detail.",
                         "stability": "beta"},
            },
            **contract_extra,
        })


def _manifest(*tools) -> AppManifest:
    specs = tools or (_tool(),)
    return AppManifest(
        slug="samplemodels", display_name="Sample", route_prefix="/samplemodels",
        job_types=tuple(spec.job_type for spec in specs), credit_cost=_cost,
        lifecycle="released", surface="customer", tools=specs)


def _fixture_apps():
    return [LoadedApp(manifest=_manifest(), router=None, error="")]


def _config(**overrides):
    return load_public_api_config({"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1",
                                   "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": TOOL, **overrides})

def _token(scopes=(SCOPE_TOOLS_READ, SCOPE_JOBS_READ), allowed_tools=()):
    from platform_core.db import get_session
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen = get_session()
    db = next(gen)
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"m-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                              password="a-good-password-12")
        db.flush()
        _key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, scopes=scopes,
                                    allowed_tools=allowed_tools,
                                    env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
        db.commit()
        return token
    finally:
        try:
            next(gen)
        except StopIteration:
            pass


def _auth(token: str) -> dict:
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    assert require_model(models, "fine").stability == "beta"

        {"models": [model.to_public_dict() for model in build_models(catalog)],
         "tools": [tool.to_public_dict() for tool in catalog]},
        ensure_ascii=False)
    for secret in ("vendor-model-swift-9", "vendor-model-fine-9", "samplemodels",
                   "samplemodels.fixture"):
        assert secret not in document, secret


#: Cụm được phép: `openai` ở đây là **tên một định dạng dây**, không phải nhà cung
#: cấp model ta bán lại. `text.chat` cố ý tương thích dây OpenAI — đó là **tính
#: năng bán cho khách**, và giấu nó đi làm tài liệu tệ hơn mà không bảo vệ gì
#: (ta không bán lại OpenAI).
#:
#: ⛔ Nhưng KHÔNG miễn trừ cả chuỗi. Chỉ bóc đúng những cụm dưới đây rồi mới dò —
#:    nên `openai` đứng một mình, hay đứng như một model/alias, VẪN đỏ.
#:    Lý lẽ đầy đủ ở `test_187::test_openai_may_be_NAMED_AS_A_FORMAT_but_never_AS_A_MODEL`.
CUM_DINH_DANG_DUOC_PHEP = ("openai format", "openai-compatible",
                           "openai compatible", "openai image_url")


def _boc_ten_dinh_dang(text: str) -> str:
    for cum in CUM_DINH_DANG_DUOC_PHEP:
        text = text.replace(cum, "<dinh-dang>")
    return text


def test_the_repository_catalog_leaks_no_vendor_name():
    """The same rule, against what this repository actually publishes."""
    everything = ",".join(sorted({
        tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
        for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS=everything))
    document = json.dumps(
        {"models": [model.to_public_dict() for model in build_models(catalog)]},
        ensure_ascii=False).lower()
    # "stability" is a field name here, so the vendor is spelled the way the
    # company is — a leak detector that trips on its own schema gets deleted.
    document = _boc_ten_dinh_dang(document)
    for vendor in ("gemini", "openai", "byteplus", "google", "anthropic",
                   "stabilityai", "stability ai", "flash", "realesrgan",
                   "whisper"):
        assert vendor not in document, vendor

# ── Schema chain ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _walk(schema: dict, path: str = "input"):
    """Yield (path, subschema) for the schema and every nested property."""
    yield path, schema
    for name, child in (schema.get("properties") or {}).items():
        yield from _walk(child, f"{path}.{name}")


def test_every_published_input_schema_is_well_formed_json_schema():
    everything = ",".join(sorted({
        tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
        for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS=everything))
    allowed_types = {"object", "string", "integer", "number", "boolean",
                     "array", "artifact", "artifact[]"}
    for tool in catalog:
        schema = tool.input_schema
        assert schema["type"] == "object"
        # Unknown fields must be refused, not ignored: silently dropping a
        # misspelled parameter is how a caller pays for a job that did not do
        # what they asked.
        assert schema["additionalProperties"] is False, tool.name
        properties = schema.get("properties") or {}
        for name in schema.get("required", ()):
            assert name in properties, f"{tool.name}: required {name} not declared"
        for path, node in _walk(schema, tool.name):
            assert node.get("type") in allowed_types, f"{path}: {node.get('type')}"
            if "enum" in node:
                assert node["enum"], f"{path}: empty enum"
                assert len(set(map(str, node["enum"]))) == len(node["enum"])
        for name, node in (tool.output_schema.get("properties") or {}).items():
            assert node.get("type") in allowed_types, f"{tool.name}.{name}"


def test_every_model_ref_parameter_publishes_its_valid_values():
    """The acceptance criterion: no public model_ref without discoverable values."""
    for item in discover():
        if item.error:
            continue
        for tool in item.manifest.tools:
            if not tool.api_exposed:
                continue
            public = project_tool(item.manifest, tool)
            hidden = set((tool.api_contract or {}).get("hidden") or ())
            for param, schema in tool.params_schema.items():
                if schema.get("type") != "model_ref" or param in hidden:
                    continue
                published = public.input_schema["properties"][param]
                assert published["enum"], f"{public.name}.{param} has no values"
                assert published["enum"] == public.model_names()


def test_the_openapi_document_carries_every_tool_schema(api):
    document = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/openapi.json").json()
    schemas = document["components"]["schemas"]
    assert f"Tool_{TOOL}_Input" in schemas
    assert f"Tool_{TOOL}_Output" in schemas
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(), apps=_fixture_apps())
    assert schemas[f"Tool_{TOOL}_Input"] == require_tool(catalog, TOOL).input_schema


def test_the_openapi_document_is_still_only_declared_routes(api):
    """Injecting schemas must not smuggle in a path."""
    from server.api.inventory import documented_paths

    document = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/openapi.json").json()
    served = {(method.upper(), f"{API_V1_PREFIX}{path}")
              for path, methods in document["paths"].items()
              for method in methods}
    assert served == documented_paths()


# ── Contract hash ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_the_contract_hash_covers_the_contract_and_not_itself():
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(), apps=_fixture_apps())
    body = require_tool(catalog, TOOL).to_public_dict()
    assert body["contract_hash"] == contract_hash(body)
    # Recomputing over the body *including* the hash would make it unverifiable.
    assert contract_hash(body) == contract_hash(
        {key: value for key, value in body.items() if key != "contract_hash"})


def test_the_contract_hash_changes_when_the_contract_does():
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(), apps=_fixture_apps())
    first = require_tool(catalog, TOOL).to_public_dict()["contract_hash"]

    changed = [LoadedApp(manifest=_manifest(_tool(description="…")),
                         router=None, error="")]
    second = require_tool(build_catalog(_config(), apps=changed),
                          TOOL).to_public_dict()["contract_hash"]
    assert first != second


def test_the_hash_a_caller_receives_is_the_hash_of_what_they_received(api):
    body = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools/{TOOL}",
                   headers=_auth(_token())).json()
    assert body["contract_hash"] == contract_hash(body)

def test_a_replacement_must_be_a_model_that_exists():

    tool = ToolSpec(

def test_a_model_alias_cannot_carry_an_undeclared_key():

def test_the_repository_publishes_a_model_for_every_alias_it_advertises():
    """Live check: the deployment's own aliases all survive the projection."""
    everything = ",".join(sorted({
        tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
        for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    catalog = build_catalog(_config(LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS=everything))
    models = {model.name for model in build_models(catalog)}
    for tool in catalog:
        assert set(tool.model_names()) <= models, tool.name
    # `image.generate` publishes these three. `pro` was closed on 2026-08-23 for a
    # commercial reason, not a technical one: its provider cost is 35.2 credits an
    # image while the platform charged 16 (taoanh) and 5 (thumbnail, flat price
    # regardless of model). See CHANGELOG.md and tests/test_261.
    assert {"standard", "standard-lite", "enhanced"} <= models
    assert "pro" not in models, "bac pro da dong — xem CHANGELOG 2026-08-23"

def _user(db, credits: int = 500):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=f"pj-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
                          password="a-good-password-12")
    db.flush()
    credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
    db.commit()
    return user


def _key(db, user, *, project=None, **kwargs):
    key, token = devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, scopes=ALL_SCOPES,
                               project_id=project.id if project else "",
                               env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER}, **kwargs)
    db.commit()
    return key, token


def _auth(token: str) -> dict:
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}


# ── Hierarchy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_project_belongs_to_one_account_and_slugs_are_unique_within_it(db):
    alice, bob = _user(db), _user(db)
    first = projects.create(db, user_id=alice.id, name="Web Site")
    second = projects.create(db, user_id=alice.id, name="Web Site")
    theirs = projects.create(db, user_id=bob.id, name="Web Site")
    db.commit()

    assert first.slug == "web-site"
    # Two integrations with the same name is a normal thing to want; refusing
    # the second teaches nothing, so it is suffixed instead.
    assert second.slug == "web-site-2"
    # …but the namespace is per account, so another customer keeps the clean one.
    assert theirs.slug == "web-site"


def test_a_vietnamese_name_becomes_a_readable_slug(db):
    """A slug exists to be read in a log line; a row of dashes is not that."""
    user = _user(db)
    project = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Trang bán hàng")
    assert project.slug == "trang-ban-hang"
    assert projects.slugify("Đội ngũ nội bộ") == "doi-ngu-noi-bo"
    # A name with nothing left after folding still gets a usable slug.
    assert projects.slugify("!!!") == "default"


def test_the_default_project_is_created_on_first_use_not_at_signup(db):
    user = _user(db)
    assert projects.list_for(db, user_id=user.id) == []
    default = projects.default_for(db, user_id=user.id)
    db.commit()
    assert default.slug == "default"
    assert projects.default_for(db, user_id=user.id).id == default.id


def test_a_key_carries_its_project_all_the_way_to_the_api(api, db):
    user = _user(db)
    project = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Batch")
    _key_row, token = _key(db, user, project=project)

    body = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers=_auth(token)).json()
    assert body["project_id"] == project.id
    assert body["account_id"] == user.id


def test_a_project_cannot_be_fetched_by_a_different_account(db):
    alice, bob = _user(db), _user(db)
    project = projects.create(db, user_id=alice.id, name="Private")
    db.commit()
    assert projects.get_owned(db, user_id=bob.id, project_id=project.id) is None
    assert projects.get_owned(db, user_id=alice.id,
                              project_id=project.id).id == project.id


def test_projects_are_capped_per_account(db, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(projects, "MAX_PROJECTS_PER_USER", 2)
    user = _user(db)
    projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="One")
    projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Two")
    with pytest.raises(projects.ProjectError):
        projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Three")


# ── Archiving ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_archiving_a_project_revokes_its_keys_and_leaves_the_others_alone(api, db):
    user = _user(db)
    retiring = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Old")
    keeping = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="New")
    _old_row, old_token = _key(db, user, project=retiring)
    _new_row, new_token = _key(db, user, project=keeping)

    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers=_auth(old_token)).status_code == 200

    revoked = projects.archive(db, retiring)
    db.commit()
    assert revoked == 1
    assert retiring.status == PROJECT_ARCHIVED

    # The retired integration stops immediately…
    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                   headers=_auth(old_token)).status_code == 401
    # …and the other one never noticed.
    assert api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                   headers=_auth(new_token)).status_code == 200


def test_archiving_destroys_no_evidence_about_money(api, db):
    """The invariant that makes archiving safe to offer at all."""
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from platform_core.models import CreditEntry, Job

    user = _user(db)
    project = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Spender")
    _row, token = _key(db, user, project=project)

    quote = api.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                     json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
                     headers=_auth(token)).json()
    created = api.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"], "input": {"prompt": "hi"}},
        headers={**_auth(token), "Idempotency-Key": "projects-spend-1"})
    assert created.status_code == 201

    def _counts():
        return (int(db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(Job.id))).scalar_one()),
                int(db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(CreditEntry.id)))
                    .scalar_one()))

    before = _counts()
    projects.archive(db, project)
    db.commit()
    assert _counts() == before
    assert before[0] == 1 and before[1] >= 1


def test_unarchiving_brings_the_project_back_but_not_the_keys(db):
    user = _user(db)
    project = projects.create(db, user_id=user.id, name="Seasonal")
    key_row, _token = _key(db, user, project=project)
    projects.archive(db, project)
    db.commit()

    projects.unarchive(db, project)
    db.commit()
    assert project.status == PROJECT_ACTIVE
    # Revocation is one-way: a credential that was announced as dead stays dead.
    assert key_row.revoked_at is not None


def test_the_default_project_comes_back_if_it_was_archived(db):
    user = _user(db)
    default = projects.default_for(db, user_id=user.id)
    projects.archive(db, default)
    db.commit()
    # Otherwise the account could no longer create a key at all.
    assert projects.default_for(db, user_id=user.id).status == PROJECT_ACTIVE


# ── Key restrictions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_an_ip_allowlist_is_stored_as_canonical_cidr(db):
    user = _user(db)
    key, _token = _key(db, user, allowed_ips=["203.0.113.4", "198.51.100.0/24",
                                              " 203.0.113.4 "])
    assert key.allowed_ips == ["203.0.113.4/32", "198.51.100.0/24"]


def test_a_nonsense_ip_is_refused_at_issue_time(db):
    user = _user(db)
    with pytest.raises(devkeys.DeveloperKeyError):
        devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id, allowed_ips=["not-an-address"],
                      env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})


@pytest.mark.parametrize("caller,allowed", [
    ("203.0.113.4", True),
    ("203.0.113.5", False),
    ("198.51.100.77", True),
    ("", False),
    ("garbage", False),
])
def test_the_allowlist_decides_by_range_and_fails_closed(db, caller, allowed):
    user = _user(db)
    key, _token = _key(db, user, allowed_ips=["203.0.113.4",
                                              "198.51.100.0/24"])
    assert devkeys.ip_allowed(key, caller) is allowed


def test_an_empty_allowlist_means_anywhere(db):
    user = _user(db)
    key, _token = _key(db, user)
    assert devkeys.ip_allowed(key, "203.0.113.4") is True
    assert devkeys.ip_allowed(key, "") is True


def test_a_key_restricted_to_another_address_is_refused_by_the_api(api, db):
    user = _user(db)
    _row, token = _key(db, user, allowed_ips=["198.51.100.0/24"])
    # TestClient presents as testclient/127.0.0.1, which is outside the range.
    denied = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers=_auth(token))
    assert denied.status_code == 401
    # Same body as every other credential failure: telling the caller "right
    # key, wrong address" confirms the key is real to whoever stole it.
    assert denied.json()["code"] == "unauthorized"


def test_a_key_restricted_to_the_calling_address_still_works(api, db):
    user = _user(db)
    _row, token = _key(db, user, allowed_ips=["127.0.0.1/32"])
    # A real peer address, because the default TestClient peer is the literal
    # string "testclient" — which is exactly the "address cannot be determined"
    # case the allowlist is supposed to refuse.
    with TestClient(api.app, client=("127.0.0.1", 40001)) as caller:
        assert caller.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                          headers=_auth(token)).status_code == 200


def test_expiry_is_enforced_and_bounded(db):
    user = _user(db)
    soon = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=1)
    key, _token = _key(db, user, expires_at=soon)
    assert key.is_usable() is True
    assert key.is_usable(now=soon + timedelta(seconds=1)) is False

    with pytest.raises(devkeys.DeveloperKeyError):
        devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id,
                      expires_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1),
                      env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})
    with pytest.raises(devkeys.DeveloperKeyError):
        devkeys.issue(db, user_id=user.id,
                      expires_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=400),
                      env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})


# ── Trusted proxy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@pytest.mark.parametrize("peer,trusted", [
    ("127.0.0.1", True),
    ("::1", True),
    ("173.245.48.9", True),          # inside the configured CIDR
    ("173.245.49.9", False),         # just outside it
    ("203.0.113.7", False),
    ("garbage", False),
])
def test_trusted_proxies_accept_ranges_as_well_as_addresses(peer, trusted):
    configured = ("127.0.0.1", "::1", "173.245.48.0/24")
    assert is_trusted_peer(peer, configured) is trusted


def test_an_unparseable_trust_entry_widens_nothing():
    """A typo in a config file must not turn into "believe everyone"."""
    assert is_trusted_peer("203.0.113.7", ("not-a-cidr",)) is False
    assert is_trusted_peer("203.0.113.7", ("0.0.0.0/33",)) is False


def test_a_forwarded_address_is_only_believed_from_a_trusted_peer(api, db):
    """The header decides the allowlist outcome only when the peer is trusted."""
    user = _user(db)
    _row, token = _key(db, user, allowed_ips=["198.51.100.7/32"])
    forwarded = {**_auth(token), "CF-Connecting-IP": "198.51.100.7"}

    # From loopback — a trusted proxy by default — the header is believed, and
    # the key is allowed through on the strength of it.
    with TestClient(api.app, client=("127.0.0.1", 40002)) as trusted:
        assert trusted.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                           headers=forwarded).status_code == 200
        other = {**_auth(token), "CF-Connecting-IP": "198.51.100.8"}
        assert trusted.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                           headers=other).status_code == 401

    # From anywhere else the same header is ignored, so the caller is judged by
    # its real address and refused. Otherwise an IP allowlist would be bypassable
    # by anyone who can reach the process directly.
    with TestClient(api.app, client=("203.0.113.9", 40003)) as untrusted:
        assert untrusted.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me",
                             headers=forwarded).status_code == 401


# ── Migration safety ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_key_without_a_project_keeps_working(api, db):
    """The V2 data shape, still valid: project_id is nullable for a reason."""
    user = _user(db)
    key, token = _key(db, user)
    assert key.project_id is None
    response = api.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/me", headers=_auth(token))
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["project_id"] == ""


def test_the_migration_backfills_a_default_project_for_existing_keys(db):
    """What the migration does, expressed against the same tables it touches."""
    import sqlalchemy as sa

    user = _user(db)
    key, _token = _key(db, user)
    assert key.project_id is None

    # This is the backfill, in the same order the migration performs it.
    project = projects.default_for(db, user_id=user.id)
    db.execute(sa.text(
        "UPDATE developer_api_keys SET project_id = :pid "
        "WHERE user_id = :uid AND project_id IS NULL"),
        {"pid": project.id, "uid": user.id})
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(key)

    assert key.project_id == project.id
    assert db.execute(sa.select(sa.func.count(ApiProject.id)).where(
        ApiProject.user_id == user.id)).scalar_one() == 1

def _csrf(html: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', html)
    assert match, "no CSRF token on the page"
    return match.group(1)


def _register(client, email: str) -> None:
    """A verified account with credit, signed in."""
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.db import get_session
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen = get_session()
    db = next(gen)
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=email, password="a-good-password-12")
        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, 500, by="test")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        try:
            next(gen)
        except StopIteration:
            pass

    page = client.get("/login")
    response = client.post("/login", data={
        "username": email, "password": "a-good-password-12",
        "csrf_token": _csrf(page.text)}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert response.status_code in (302, 303), response.text

    home = portal.get("/").text
    # One click opens the account menu, the second is this link.
    assert 'href="/developers"' in home


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", BUILT)
