def test_the_navigation_is_the_same_on_every_section(portal):
    _register(portal, f"same-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com")
    links = None
    for path in BUILT:
        # Only the nav block: a section may of course link elsewhere in its body
        # (the overview's call-to-action does).
        block = re.search(r'<nav class="dev-nav".*?</nav>', portal.get(path).text,
                          re.S)
        assert block, path
        found = re.findall(r'<a href="(/developers[^"]*)"', block.group(0))
        if links is None:
            links = found
        assert found == links, path

"""EXT-06 — the variable reference: every published input, documented once.

The rule this file enforces is narrow and strict: a customer must be able to
find out what a parameter *is* without reading the app's source, and the page
that tells them must be generated from the same contract the server validates
against. Two copies of a schema is one copy that will be wrong.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.public_api import keys as devkeys, limits
from platform_core.public_api.catalog import build_catalog
from platform_core.public_api.config import load_public_api_config
from platform_core.registry import (AppManifest, LoadedApp, RegistryError,
                                    ToolSpec, discover)

PEPPER = "varref-test-pepper-" + "v" * 40


def _live_catalog():
    names = ",".join(sorted({tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
                             for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    return build_catalog(load_public_api_config(
        {"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1", "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": names}))


# ── The acceptance criterion, checked against the live repository ────────────

def test_every_published_parameter_has_a_description():
    """100% of exposed operations documented — the whole point of EXT-06."""
    missing = [(tool.name, name)
               for tool in _live_catalog()
               for name, spec in tool.input_schema["properties"].items()
               if not str(spec.get("description") or "").strip()]
    assert not missing, f"undocumented public parameters: {missing}"


def test_documentation_never_describes_a_parameter_the_api_refuses():
    """The opposite failure: prose promising an input that does not exist."""
    for item in discover():
        if item.error:
            continue
        for tool in item.manifest.tools:
            contract = tool.api_contract or {}
            documented = set(contract.get("params") or {})
            hidden = set(contract.get("hidden") or ())
            assert documented <= set(tool.params_schema), tool.name
            assert not (documented & hidden), tool.name


#: Cụm được phép: `openai` ở đây là **tên một định dạng dây**, không phải nhà cung
#: cấp model ta bán lại. `text.chat` cố ý tương thích dây OpenAI — đó là **tính
#: năng bán cho khách**, và giấu nó đi làm tài liệu tệ hơn mà không bảo vệ gì
#: (ta không bán lại OpenAI).
#:
#: ⛔ Nhưng KHÔNG miễn trừ cả chuỗi. Chỉ bóc đúng những cụm dưới đây rồi mới dò —
#:    nên `openai` đứng một mình, hay đứng như một model/alias, VẪN đỏ.
#:    Lý lẽ đầy đủ ở `test_187::test_openai_may_be_NAMED_AS_A_FORMAT_but_never_AS_A_MODEL`.
CUM_DINH_DANG_DUOC_PHEP = ("openai format", "openai-compatible",
                           "openai compatible", "openai image_url")


def _boc_ten_dinh_dang(text: str) -> str:
    for cum in CUM_DINH_DANG_DUOC_PHEP:
        text = text.replace(cum, "<dinh-dang>")
    return text


def test_the_public_docs_say_nothing_about_the_vendor():
    text = " ".join(
        str(spec.get("description", "")) + " " + str(spec.get("examples", ""))
        for tool in _live_catalog()
        for spec in tool.input_schema["properties"].values()).lower()
    text = _boc_ten_dinh_dang(text)
    for vendor in ("gemini", "openai", "byteplus", "anthropic", "realesrgan",
                   "whisper", "prompt library"):
        assert vendor not in text, vendor


# ── The contract refuses documentation that would drift ─────────────────────

def _tool_with(params) -> tuple:
    tool = ToolSpec(
        name="text.documented", job_type="sampledoc.run",
        description="Fixture tool.",
        params_schema={"prompt": {"type": "string", "required": True},
                       "secret_knob": {"type": "string"}},
        returns={"text": "text"}, api_exposed=True,
        api_contract={"scopes": ("jobs:create",), "hidden": ("secret_knob",),
                      "params": params})
    manifest = AppManifest(
        slug="sampledoc", display_name="Sample", route_prefix="/sampledoc",
        job_types=("sampledoc.run",), credit_cost=lambda params: 1,
        lifecycle="released", surface="customer", tools=(tool,))
    return manifest, tool


def test_documenting_an_unknown_parameter_is_refused():
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest, tool = _tool_with({"ghost": {"description": "nope"}})
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError) as raised:
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, tool)
    assert "ghost" in str(raised.value)


def test_documenting_a_hidden_parameter_is_refused():
    """A caller cannot send it, so describing it is a promise nobody keeps."""
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest, tool = _tool_with({"secret_knob": {"description": "internal"}})
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError) as raised:
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, tool)
    assert "secret_knob" in str(raised.value)


def test_an_empty_description_is_refused():
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest, tool = _tool_with({"prompt": {"example": "hello"}})
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError):
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, tool)


def test_an_unknown_documentation_key_is_refused():
    from platform_core.registry import _validate_api_contract

    manifest, tool = _tool_with({"prompt": {"description": "ok",
                                            "internal_note": "leak"}})
    with pytest.raises(RegistryError) as raised:
        _validate_api_contract(manifest, tool)
    assert "internal_note" in str(raised.value)


def test_the_description_reaches_the_published_schema():
    manifest, _tool = _tool_with({"prompt": {"description": "What to write.",
                                             "example": "a haiku"}})
    catalog = build_catalog(
        load_public_api_config({"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1",
                                "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": "text.documented"}),
        apps=[LoadedApp(manifest=manifest, router=None, error="")])
    published = catalog[0].input_schema["properties"]["prompt"]
    assert published["description"] == "What to write."
    # JSON Schema 2020-12 spells this `examples`, and it is a list.
    assert published["examples"] == ["a haiku"]
    assert "secret_knob" not in catalog[0].input_schema["properties"]

    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.db import get_session
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    gen = get_session()

    try:

        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, 100, by="test")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        try:
            next(gen)
        except StopIteration:
            pass

    page = client.get("/login").text
    token = re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', page).group(1)
    client.post("/login", data={"username": email,
                                "password": "a-good-password-12",
                                "csrf_token": token}, follow_redirects=False)

"""EXT-07 — the quickstart: a fresh integration that actually completes.

Two failure modes are worth testing here and only two. An example that no longer
matches the schema is worse than no example, because a developer trusts it and
loses an afternoon. And an example carrying a real credential is a leak that
ships with the documentation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.public_api import examples, keys as devkeys, limits
from platform_core.public_api.catalog import build_catalog
from platform_core.public_api.config import load_public_api_config
from platform_core.registry import (AppManifest, LoadedApp, ToolSpec, discover)
from server.api.inventory import API_V1_PREFIX, declared_paths

PEPPER = "quickstart-test-pepper-" + "q" * 40


def _live_catalog():
    names = ",".join(sorted({tool.name for item in discover() if not item.error
                             for tool in item.manifest.tools}))
    return build_catalog(load_public_api_config(
        {"LTT_PUBLIC_API": "1", "LTT_PUBLIC_API_TOOLS": names}))


def _snippets(tool) -> dict:
    return {
        "curl_quote": examples.curl_quote(tool),
        "curl_submit": examples.curl_submit(tool),
        "python": examples.python_snippet(tool),
        "typescript": examples.typescript_snippet(tool),
        "powershell": examples.powershell_snippet(tool),
        "http": examples.raw_http_snippet(tool),
    }


# ── Examples match the schema they claim to call ─────────────────────────────

def _violations(payload: dict, schema: dict) -> list:
    """A small schema check: the published contract is a narrow subset of JSON
    Schema, so a dependency to validate it would be more surface than value."""
    problems = []
    properties = schema.get("properties") or {}
    for name in schema.get("required", ()):
        if name not in payload:
            problems.append(f"missing required {name}")
    for name, value in payload.items():
        if name not in properties:
            problems.append(f"unknown field {name}")
            continue
        spec = properties[name]
        placeholder = isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("<")
        expected = spec.get("type")
        if not placeholder:
            if expected == "integer" and not isinstance(value, int):
                problems.append(f"{name} should be an integer")
            if expected == "string" and not isinstance(value, str):
                problems.append(f"{name} should be a string")
            if spec.get("enum") and value not in spec["enum"]:
                problems.append(f"{name}={value!r} is not in the enum")
            if isinstance(value, str) and "maxLength" in spec:
                if len(value) > spec["maxLength"]:
                    problems.append(f"{name} is longer than maxLength")
            if isinstance(value, int) and "minimum" in spec:
                if value < spec["minimum"]:
                    problems.append(f"{name} below minimum")
            if isinstance(value, int) and "maximum" in spec:
                if value > spec["maximum"]:
                    problems.append(f"{name} above maximum")
    return problems


def test_every_example_payload_validates_against_its_own_tool_schema():
    for tool in _live_catalog():
        payload = examples.example_input(tool)
        assert not _violations(payload, tool.input_schema), tool.name


def test_the_example_payload_would_be_accepted_by_the_real_submit_path():
    """The same validation the chargeable route runs, not a lookalike."""
    from platform_core.public_api.invocation import validate_public_input

    for tool in _live_catalog():
        # The whole payload, exactly as the page prints it. Media ids are only
        # resolved to real uploads later, so a placeholder id is a valid input
        # as far as this layer is concerned — which is the layer that decides
        # whether a caller pasting the example gets a 400.
        validate_public_input(tool, examples.example_input(tool))


def test_every_snippet_only_calls_endpoints_that_exist():
    declared = {path for _method, path in declared_paths()}
    for tool in _live_catalog():
        for label, snippet in _snippets(tool).items():
            for path in set(re.findall(r"/api/v1/[a-z/{}_]+", snippet)):
                clean = path.rstrip("/")
                # Snippets use readable placeholders; the inventory uses the
                # route's own parameter names.
                normalised = re.sub(r"\{[a-z_]+\}", "{x}", clean)
                known = {re.sub(r"\{[a-z_]+\}", "{x}", item)
                         for item in declared}
                assert normalised in known, f"{tool.name}/{label}: {path}"


def test_no_snippet_contains_anything_that_looks_like_a_key():
    """A credential in an example ships with the documentation forever."""
    for tool in _live_catalog():
        for label, snippet in _snippets(tool).items():
            assert "ltt_sk_" not in snippet.replace("ltt_sk_…", ""), label
            # …and every snippet must read the key from the environment.
            assert examples.ENV_API_KEY in snippet, f"{tool.name}/{label}"


def test_the_chargeable_snippets_carry_an_idempotency_key():
    for tool in _live_catalog():
        snippets = _snippets(tool)
        for label in ("curl_submit", "python", "typescript", "powershell",
                      "http"):
            assert "Idempotency-Key" in snippets[label], f"{tool.name}/{label}"
        # …and the quote call does not pretend to need one.
        assert "Idempotency-Key" not in snippets["curl_quote"]


def test_the_environment_variables_are_named_once_and_used_everywhere():
    assert (examples.ENV_API_KEY, examples.ENV_BASE_URL) == ("LTT_API_KEY",
                                                             "LTT_BASE_URL")
    names = {name for name, _sample, _why in examples.ENV_VARS}
    assert names == {"LTT_API_KEY", "LTT_BASE_URL", "LTT_PROJECT_ID"}
    for _shell, snippet in examples.SHELL_EXPORTS:
        assert "LTT_BASE_URL" in snippet and "LTT_API_KEY" in snippet

    tool = ToolSpec(
        name="text.placeheld", job_type="samplehold.run", description="Fixture.",
        params_schema={"needed": {"type": "string", "required": True}},

def _csrf(html: str) -> str:
    return re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', html).group(1)


def _sign_in(client) -> str:
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.db import get_session
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    email = f"qs-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    gen = get_session()
    db = next(gen)
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=email, password="a-good-password-12")
        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, 200, by="test")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        try:
            next(gen)
        except StopIteration:
            pass
    page = client.get("/login").text
    client.post("/login", data={"username": email,
                                "password": "a-good-password-12",
                                "csrf_token": _csrf(page)},
                follow_redirects=False)
    return email

# ── The acceptance criterion: a fresh integration completes ──────────────────

def test_a_developer_who_follows_the_quickstart_gets_a_result(portal):
    """Portal → key → env → tools → quote → job → artifact, in that order.

    This is the whole promise of EXT-07 expressed as a test: if any step of the
    documented path stops working, this fails.
    """
    _sign_in(portal)

    # Step 1-2: create the key exactly as the page says to.
    keys_page = portal.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = portal.post("/developers/keys", data={
        "name": "quickstart", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
        "scopes": ["tools:read", "jobs:create", "jobs:read", "artifacts:read"]})
    token = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text).group(1)
    auth = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    # Step 4: discover.
    tools = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=auth).json()
    published = [item["name"] for item in tools["items"]]
    assert "image.thumbnail" in published

    # Step 6: quote, then submit with an idempotency key.
    catalog_tool = next(item for item in _live_catalog()
                        if item.name == "image.thumbnail")
    payload = examples.example_input(catalog_tool)
    quote = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": "image.thumbnail", "input": payload},
                        headers=auth)
    assert quote.status_code == 200, quote.text
    assert quote.json()["credit"] > 0

    job = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                      json={"tool": "image.thumbnail",
                            "quote": quote.json()["quote"], "input": payload},
                      headers={**auth, "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())})
    assert job.status_code == 201, job.text

    # Step 7: the job runs and its artifact is fetchable.
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job

    assert _chay_mot_job("quickstart-worker") is True

    finished = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/{job.json()['id']}",
                          headers=auth).json()
    assert finished["status"] == "succeeded", finished
    #  is a list of artifact descriptors, one per produced file.
    artifact = finished["outputs"][0]["id"]
    detail = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/artifacts/{artifact}", headers=auth)
    assert detail.status_code == 200, detail.text

"""
Tests for the TikTokPublisher rate-limit integration (Phase 5 fix).

Before the fix, rate_limiter was accepted as a parameter but completely ignored
inside TikTokPublisher — meaning all of the anti-ban mechanisms (per-account
interval, daily quota, jitter, active hours) silently didn't apply to TikTok
uploads. These tests lock that behaviour in place going forward.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import unittest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from core.rate_limiter import QuotaExceededError, RateLimiter, reset_global_metrics
from core.tiktok.publisher_service import TikTokPublisher
from core.tiktok.token_store import TikTokAccount


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Helpers
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _make_account(open_id="u1", display_name="TestUser"):
    """Construct a minimal TikTokAccount sufficient for publish() exercises."""
    import time
    future = time.time() + 30 * 24 * 3600
    return TikTokAccount(
        open_id            = open_id,
        display_name       = display_name,
        avatar_url         = "",
        access_token       = "fake_access_token",
        refresh_token      = "fake_refresh",
        expires_at         = future,
        refresh_expires_at = future,
        scopes             = ["user.info.basic", "video.upload", "video.publish"],
    )


def _make_publisher(rate_limiter=None, audit_approved=True):
    """Spawn a TikTokPublisher with a stub stop_event and minimal config."""
    config = {
        "tiktok_audit_approved":    audit_approved,
        "tiktok_enable_direct_post": True,
        "tiktok_request_timeout_s": 5,
    }
    return TikTokPublisher(
        config       = config,
        stop_event   = threading.Event(),
        on_log       = lambda m, l: None,
        on_status    = lambda m: None,
        rate_limiter = rate_limiter,
    )


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Publisher stores the rate_limiter (no longer "ignored")
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestRateLimiterAccepted(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        reset_global_metrics()

    def test_publisher_keeps_rate_limiter_reference(self):
        rl = RateLimiter(min_interval_s=0.0)
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=rl)
        self.assertIs(pub._rate_limiter, rl)

    def test_publisher_accepts_none_for_back_compat(self):
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=None)
        self.assertIsNone(pub._rate_limiter)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. acquire/release happens during publish — checked via direct invocation
#    of the rate limiter's daily counters (no need to mock the upload path).
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestPublishCallsAcquireRelease(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        reset_global_metrics()

    def test_publish_increments_account_daily_count(self):
        """A successful publish must release() → which bumps account_daily_count.
        We mock everything past compliance check to avoid touching network."""
        rl = RateLimiter(min_interval_s=0.0)
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=rl)

        account = _make_account(open_id="u_quota_test", display_name="QT")

        # Mock the inner pipeline so publish() returns without network I/O
        pub._resolve_account     = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._ensure_token_fresh  = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._upload_draft        = MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock(
            success=True, external_post_id="pid_1", status="draft",
        ))

        with patch(
            "core.tiktok.compliance_guard.TikTokComplianceGuard.check",
            return_value=[],
        ):
            pub.publish({
                "video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4",
                "post_type":  "tiktok_draft",
            })

        self.assertEqual(rl.account_daily_count("u_quota_test"), 1)

    def test_publish_releases_even_on_exception(self):
        """If upload raises, release() must still be called so the slot is
        freed and the daily counter still increments (penalises a failed
        attempt the same way as a success — protects against retry loops)."""
        rl = RateLimiter(min_interval_s=0.0)
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=rl)

        account = _make_account(open_id="u_err_test", display_name="ER")
        pub._resolve_account    = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._ensure_token_fresh = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._upload_draft       = MagicMock(side_effect=RuntimeError("boom"))

        with patch(
            "core.tiktok.compliance_guard.TikTokComplianceGuard.check",
            return_value=[],
        ):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                pub.publish({
                    "video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4",
                    "post_type":  "tiktok_draft",
                })

        # Even on failure, release ran → daily count = 1
        self.assertEqual(rl.account_daily_count("u_err_test"), 1)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 3. Quota enforcement actually blocks TikTok publishes
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestTikTokQuotaEnforced(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        reset_global_metrics()

    def test_per_account_quota_blocks_third_attempt(self):
        rl = RateLimiter(
            min_interval_s=0.0,
            max_posts_per_account_per_day=2,
        )
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=rl)
        account = _make_account(open_id="u_cap", display_name="Capped")
        pub._resolve_account    = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._ensure_token_fresh = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._upload_draft       = MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock(
            success=True, external_post_id="pid", status="draft",
        ))

        with patch(
            "core.tiktok.compliance_guard.TikTokComplianceGuard.check",
            return_value=[],
        ):
            # 2 successful publishes — within cap
            pub.publish({"video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4", "post_type": "tiktok_draft"})
            pub.publish({"video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4", "post_type": "tiktok_draft"})
            # 3rd → QuotaExceededError before any network call
            with self.assertRaises(QuotaExceededError):
                pub.publish({"video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4", "post_type": "tiktok_draft"})


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 4. Back-compat: rate_limiter=None still works (legacy path)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestNoneRateLimiterBackCompat(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        reset_global_metrics()

    def test_publish_without_limiter_doesnt_crash(self):
        """Tests that pre-existed (test_15_tiktok_commenter) called the publisher
        with rate_limiter=None and expected nothing weird to happen."""
        pub = _make_publisher(rate_limiter=None)
        account = _make_account(open_id="u_none")
        pub._resolve_account    = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._ensure_token_fresh = MagicMock(return_value=account)
        pub._upload_draft       = MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock(
            success=True, external_post_id="pid", status="draft",
        ))

        with patch(
            "core.tiktok.compliance_guard.TikTokComplianceGuard.check",
            return_value=[],
        ):
            result = pub.publish({
                "video_path": "/tmp/x.mp4",
                "post_type":  "tiktok_draft",
            })
        # No exception, returns the mocked result — confirming None path works
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# ── No private execution path ────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_the_portal_has_no_route_that_runs_a_tool(portal):
    """The playground must not become a second road to the chargeable path.

    Every way to spend credit stays on `/api/v1`, where the quote, the
    idempotency key, the limits and the ledger already live.
    """
    _sign_in(portal)
    routes = [route.path for route in portal.app.routes
              if str(getattr(route, "path", "")).startswith("/developers")]
    for path in routes:
        assert "run" not in path and "execute" not in path, path
        assert "quote" not in path, path


def test_the_page_talks_to_the_public_api_and_nothing_else():
    source = SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    called = set(re.findall(r'fetch\("([^"]+)"', source))
    called |= set(re.findall(r'fetch\("(/api/v1[^"]*)"', source))
    for target in called:
        assert target.startswith("/api/v1"), target
    # …and every path it builds exists in the route inventory.
    declared = {re.sub(r"\{[a-z_]+\}", "{x}", path)
                for _method, path in declared_paths()}
    for path in re.findall(r'"/(?:api/v1)?(/[a-z/]+)"', source):
        candidate = re.sub(r"\{[a-z_]+\}", "{x}", API_V1_PREFIX + path)
        if candidate.endswith(("/quotes", "/jobs", "/uploads")):
            assert candidate in declared, path


# ── No raw key recovery ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_the_page_never_contains_a_key_and_never_stores_one(portal):
    """The customer was told a key cannot be recovered. That has to stay true."""
    _sign_in(portal)
    keys_page = portal.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = portal.post("/developers/keys", data={
        "name": "playground", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
        "scopes": ["tools:read", "jobs:create", "jobs:read", "artifacts:read"]})
    token = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text).group(1)

    page = portal.get("/developers/playground").text
    assert token not in page
    assert "ltt_sk_" not in page.replace("ltt_sk_…", "")
    # The field is a password input and the script keeps the value in memory.
    assert 'id="pg-key" type="password"' in page
    # Comments stripped first: the file *explains* that it never uses these,
    # and a scan that trips on its own documentation is a scan people delete.
    source = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                    flags=re.S)
    source = re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", source, flags=re.M)
    for forbidden in ("localStorage", "sessionStorage", "document.cookie"):
        assert forbidden not in source, forbidden


def test_the_server_never_receives_the_key_from_the_page(portal):
    """Nothing in the page posts back to the portal, so there is nothing for a
    portal handler to log, store or leak."""
    _sign_in(portal)
    page = portal.get("/developers/playground").text
    assert 'action="/developers' not in page.split('id="playground"')[1]

    assert embedded == published

def test_the_page_says_the_run_costs_real_credit(portal):
    """There is no free mode, and pretending otherwise would be the bypass."""

def test_the_page_generates_an_idempotency_key_and_reuses_it_per_call():
    source = SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "Idempotency-Key" in source
    # Generated once per call…
    assert "state.idempotencyKey = uuid()" in source.replace(
        "(state.idempotencyKey = uuid())", "state.idempotencyKey = uuid()")
    # …and thrown away when the input changes, because that is a different call
    # and replaying the old answer would be wrong.
    assert "state.idempotencyKey = null" in source


def test_the_inspector_shows_only_headers_a_caller_should_act_on():
    source = SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    shown = set(re.findall(r'"([A-Za-z-]+)"', safe))
    assert shown == {"X-Correlation-ID", "X-LTT-API-Version", "Retry-After",
                     "Idempotency-Replayed", "Location"}
    # Nothing that would echo a credential back onto the page.
    assert "Authorization" not in safe

# ── The semantics the page relies on are the API's, not its own ─────────────

def test_running_from_a_form_is_the_same_call_as_running_from_a_server(portal):
    """What the page does, done here with plain requests: identical outcome.

    If these two ever diverge, the playground is lying to whoever trusts it.
    """
    _sign_in(portal)
    keys_page = portal.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = portal.post("/developers/keys", data={
        "name": "same-path", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
        "scopes": ["tools:read", "jobs:create", "jobs:read"]})
    token = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text).group(1)
    auth = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    payload = {"topic": "playground parity", "count": 1}

    quote = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": "image.thumbnail", "input": payload},
                        headers=auth)
    assert quote.status_code == 200
    key = str(uuid.uuid4())
    first = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                        json={"tool": "image.thumbnail",
                              "quote": quote.json()["quote"], "input": payload},
                        headers={**auth, "Idempotency-Key": key})
    assert first.status_code == 201

    # Pressing Run twice with the same input replays rather than charging again
    # — the behaviour the page depends on by reusing its key.
    again = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                        json={"tool": "image.thumbnail",
                              "quote": quote.json()["quote"], "input": payload},
                        headers={**auth, "Idempotency-Key": key})
    assert again.status_code == 200
    assert again.json()["id"] == first.json()["id"]
    assert again.headers.get("Idempotency-Replayed") == "true"

"""EXT-09 — request logs: a developer debugging their own calls.

The acceptance is specific: 401, 403, 409, 422, 429, 5xx and a failed job must
all be explainable afterwards. Everything else here defends the two properties
that make such a log safe to keep — it holds no payload, and it never shows one

def _session():
    from platform_core.db import get_session

    gen = get_session()
    return gen, next(gen)


def _close(gen):
    try:
        next(gen)
    except StopIteration:
        pass


def _csrf(html: str) -> str:
    return re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', html).group(1)


def _account(client, credits: int = 100, scopes=SCOPES):
    """A signed-in account with a key, the way a real developer starts."""
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    email = f"rl-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=email, password="a-good-password-12")
        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
        db.commit()
        user_id = user.id
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    page = client.get("/login").text
    client.post("/login", data={"username": email,
                                "password": "a-good-password-12",
                                "csrf_token": _csrf(page)},
                follow_redirects=False)
    keys_page = client.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = client.post("/developers/keys",
                          data={"name": "logs", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
                                "scopes": list(scopes)})
    found = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text)
    assert found, "key creation did not reveal a token"
    return user_id, found.group(1)


def _auth(token, idem=""):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    if idem:
        headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idem
    return headers


def _rows(user_id: str) -> list:
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        return request_log.list_for(db, user_id=user_id, limit=100)
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _quote(client, token, count=1):
    return client.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                       json={"tool": TOOL,
                             "input": {"topic": "logs", "count": count}},
                       headers=_auth(token))


# ── Every failure class is explainable afterwards ───────────────────────────

def test_the_log_records_what_changed_or_refused_something(portal):
    """The recording rule, stated as behaviour.

    A row per request cost 177 rps → 42.6 rps on the load harness, and the
    volume was almost entirely successful polling — traffic a developer can
    already see, because the job explains itself. So: every failure, and every
    call that was not a read.
    """
    user_id, token = _account(portal)

    read = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
    assert read.status_code == 200
    assert _rows(user_id) == [], "a successful read is not worth a row"

    quote = _quote(portal, token)
    assert quote.status_code == 200
    rows = _rows(user_id)
    assert len(rows) == 1
    row = rows[0]
    assert row.status == 200 and row.route.endswith("/quotes")
    assert row.request_id == quote.headers["X-Correlation-ID"]
    assert row.latency_ms >= 0

    # …and a failed read is recorded, because that is the one a developer comes
    # looking for.
    missing = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs/nope", headers=_auth(token))
    assert missing.status_code == 404
    assert any(item.status == 404 for item in _rows(user_id))


def test_a_missing_scope_is_recorded_with_its_code(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal, scopes=("jobs:read",))
    denied = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
    assert denied.status_code == 403

    row = _rows(user_id)[0]
    assert row.status == 403 and row.code == "missing_scope"


def test_running_out_of_credit_is_recorded_as_its_own_code(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal, credits=1)
    quote = _quote(portal, token)
    refused = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                          json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"],
                                "input": {"topic": "logs", "count": 1}},
                          headers=_auth(token, "reqlog-broke-1"))
    assert refused.status_code == 409

    codes = [row.code for row in _rows(user_id)]
    assert "insufficient_credit" in codes


def test_a_malformed_body_is_recorded(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    bad = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                      json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"nope": 1}},
                      headers=_auth(token))
    assert bad.status_code in (400, 422)
    assert _rows(user_id)[0].code in ("invalid_request", "unprocessable_request")


def test_hitting_the_rate_limit_is_recorded(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    for _ in range(60):
        response = portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools", headers=_auth(token))
        if response.status_code == 429:
            break
    assert response.status_code == 429
    assert any(row.status == 429 for row in _rows(user_id))


def test_a_call_with_no_credential_is_not_recorded_against_anyone(portal):
    """A row with no owner belongs to nobody and could only be shown to
    everybody. Anonymous failures stay in the operator's log."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _quote(portal, token)
    before = len(_rows(user_id))
    assert portal.get(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/tools").status_code == 401

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        from sqlalchemy import func, select
        total = int(db.execute(
            select(func.count(ApiRequestLog.id))).scalar_one())
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert len(_rows(user_id)) == before
    assert total == before


def test_a_failed_job_is_traceable_from_the_request_that_created_it(portal,
                                                                    monkeypatch):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    quote = _quote(portal, token)
    created = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                          json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"],
                                "input": {"topic": "logs", "count": 1}},
                          headers=_auth(token, "reqlog-fail-1"))
    assert created.status_code == 201
    job_id = created.json()["id"]

    import apps.thumbnail.jobs as thumbnail_jobs
    monkeypatch.setattr(thumbnail_jobs, "_goi_gemini",
                        lambda *a, **k: (_ for _ in ()).throw(
                            RuntimeError("provider said no")))
    # A failed provider call is retried with a backoff, so one pass leaves the
    # job queued again and the next pass finds nothing until the delay expires.
    # Bring `next_run_at` forward instead of sleeping: the point of the test is
    # the terminal state, not the wait.
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    from platform_core.models import Job

    for _ in range(5):
        if not _chay_mot_job("reqlog-worker"):
            gen, db = _session()
            try:
                job = db.get(Job, job_id)
                if job.status != "queued":
                    break
                job.next_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
                db.commit()
            finally:
                _close(gen)
            continue

    row = next(item for item in _rows(user_id) if item.job_id == job_id)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        timeline = request_log.timeline(db, row)
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert timeline["job"] is not None and timeline["job"].status == "error"
    # The refund is part of the story, and it is in the ledger already.
    assert any(entry.delta > 0 for entry in timeline["credit"])


def test_a_finished_job_links_request_to_events_credit_and_artifacts(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    quote = _quote(portal, token)
    created = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
                          json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"],
                                "input": {"topic": "logs", "count": 1}},
                          headers=_auth(token, "reqlog-ok-1"))
    assert created.status_code == 201
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    assert _chay_mot_job("reqlog-worker-2") is True

    row = next(item for item in _rows(user_id)
               if item.job_id == created.json()["id"])
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        timeline = request_log.timeline(db, row)
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert timeline["job"].status == "done"
    assert timeline["artifacts"], "a finished image job has an artifact"
    assert any(entry.kind for entry in timeline["credit"])


def test_the_job_carries_the_request_id_that_created_it(portal):
    """Trace propagation: API → job → worker events, with no new identifier."""
    from platform_core.public_api.invocation import api_meta
    from platform_core.models import Job

    _user_id, token = _account(portal)
    quote = _quote(portal, token)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        job = db.get(Job, created.json()["id"])
        assert api_meta(job)["request_id"] == created.headers["X-Correlation-ID"]
    finally:
        _close(gen)

def test_old_rows_are_purged_and_recent_ones_are_not(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _quote(portal, token)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        old = request_log.record(
            db, request_id="old-" + uuid.uuid4().hex, user_id=user_id,
            method="GET", route="/api/v1/me", status=200,
            now=datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=90))
        db.commit()

        db.commit()
        assert removed == 1
        assert db.get(ApiRequestLog, old.id) is None
        assert request_log.list_for(db, user_id=user_id)
    finally:
        _close(gen)

"""EXT-10 — webhook console: resend, test, rotate, and the rules behind them.

The dangerous operation here is resend. A support conversation that ends in
"just resend it" must not be able to re-run work, re-charge a customer, or make
a receiver process the same event twice — and those are three different
mistakes, so they get three different tests.

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.public_api import (keys as devkeys, limits, webhook_console,
                                      webhooks)

                                             WebhookDelivery,
                                             WebhookSubscription)
from server.api.inventory import API_V1_PREFIX

PEPPER = "console-test-pepper-" + "c" * 40
TOOL = "image.thumbnail"
RECEIVER = "https://receiver.example.com/hook"


def _public_dns(host: str) -> list:
    """Resolve the test receiver without depending on somebody else's DNS.

    The production path resolves for real and refuses a host it cannot resolve;
    the SSRF rules themselves are exercised with explicit resolvers below.
    """
    if host.endswith("example.com"):
        return ["93.184.216.34"]
    raise OSError(f"unknown test host: {host}")

    monkeypatch.setenv("LTT_DATA_DIR", str(tmp_path / "data"))

    monkeypatch.setenv("LTT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY",
                       "console-encryption-key-0123456789")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "stub-key-not-used")
    limits.reset()

    import platform_core.db as dbmod
    import platform_core.storage as storage_mod
    dbmod.reset_engine()
    storage_mod.set_storage(storage_mod.LocalStorage(str(tmp_path / "files")))
    import platform_core.models  # noqa: F401
    from platform_core.db import Base, get_engine

    Base.metadata.create_all(get_engine())

def _session():
    from platform_core.db import get_session

    gen = get_session()
    return gen, next(gen)


def _close(gen):
    try:
        next(gen)
    except StopIteration:
        pass


def _csrf(html: str) -> str:
    return re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', html).group(1)


def _account(client, scopes=("tools:read", "jobs:create", "jobs:read",
                             "webhooks:manage")):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    email = f"wc-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=email, password="a-good-password-12")
        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, 200, by="test")
        db.commit()
        user_id = user.id
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    page = client.get("/login").text
    client.post("/login", data={"username": email,
                                "password": "a-good-password-12",
                                "csrf_token": _csrf(page)},
                follow_redirects=False)
    keys_page = client.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = client.post("/developers/keys",
                          data={"name": "console", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
                                "scopes": list(scopes)})
    token = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text).group(1)
    return user_id, token


def _subscribe(client, token, url: str = RECEIVER):
    response = client.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks",
                           json={"url": url},
                           headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    assert response.status_code in (200, 201), response.text
    return response.json()


def _delivery_rows(user_id: str) -> list:
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        return webhook_console.deliveries_for(db, user_id=user_id)
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _post(client, path: str) -> None:
    page = client.get("/developers/webhooks").text
    client.post(path, data={"csrf_token": _csrf(page)}, follow_redirects=False)


# ── Resend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _finished_job_with_delivery(client, token, user_id):
    """One real job that ran, and the delivery its terminal state queued."""
    quote = client.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": TOOL, "input": {"topic": "hook", "count": 1}},
                        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}).json()
    created = client.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"],
              "input": {"topic": "hook", "count": 1}},
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                 "Idempotency-Key": f"console-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"})
    assert created.status_code == 201
    from platform_core.job_runner import _chay_mot_job
    assert _chay_mot_job("console-worker") is True
    rows = _delivery_rows(user_id)
    assert rows, "a finished job queues a delivery"
    return created.json()["id"], rows[0]


def test_resend_reuses_the_event_id_and_payload(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, token)
    _job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)
    before = {"event_id": delivery.event_id,
              "payload": dict(delivery.payload or {})}

    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/deliveries/{delivery.id}/resend")

    after = _delivery_rows(user_id)[0]
    assert after.id == delivery.id, "the row is reused, not copied"
    assert after.event_id == before["event_id"]
    assert after.status == WEBHOOK_PENDING and after.attempts == 0
    # The receiver deduplicates on the event id; a fresh id would defeat that.
    assert after.payload["id"] == before["payload"]["id"]
    assert after.payload["type"] == before["payload"]["type"]
    assert after.payload["_resends"] == 1


def test_resend_touches_neither_the_job_nor_the_ledger(portal):
    """The rule that makes 'just resend it' safe to say out loud."""
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from platform_core.models import CreditEntry, Job

    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, token)
    job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)

    def _snapshot():
        gen, db = _session()
        try:
            job = db.get(Job, job_id)
            ledger = db.execute(sa.select(CreditEntry).where(
                CreditEntry.user_id == user_id).order_by(
                    CreditEntry.created_at)).scalars().all()
            return (job.status, job.attempts,
                    [(entry.kind, entry.delta) for entry in ledger])
        finally:
            _close(gen)

    before = _snapshot()
    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/deliveries/{delivery.id}/resend")
    assert _snapshot() == before


def test_a_dead_delivery_can_be_revived(portal):
    """The case the button exists for: the receiver was down all afternoon."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, token)
    _job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        row = db.get(WebhookDelivery, delivery.id)
        row.status = WEBHOOK_DEAD
        row.attempts = webhooks.MAX_ATTEMPTS
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/deliveries/{delivery.id}/resend")
    after = _delivery_rows(user_id)[0]
    assert after.status == WEBHOOK_PENDING and after.attempts == 0


def test_resend_is_rate_limited(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, token)
    _job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        row = db.get(WebhookDelivery, delivery.id)
        payload = dict(row.payload or {})
        payload["_resends"] = webhook_console.RESEND_LIMIT_PER_HOUR
        payload["_resent_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        row.payload = payload
        db.commit()
        with pytest.raises(webhook_console.WebhookConsoleError):
            webhook_console.resend(db, row)
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_resend_only_works_on_your_own_delivery(portal):
    first_id, first_token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, first_token)
    _job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, first_token, first_id)

    portal.post("/logout", data={}, follow_redirects=False)
    _second_id, _second_token = _account(portal)
    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/deliveries/{delivery.id}/resend")

    after = _delivery_rows(first_id)[0]
    assert "_resends" not in (after.payload or {})


# ── Test event ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_test_event_says_it_is_a_test_and_costs_nothing(portal):
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from platform_core.models import CreditEntry, Job

    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    subscription = _subscribe(portal, token)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        jobs_before = int(db.execute(
            sa.select(sa.func.count(Job.id))).scalar_one())
        ledger_before = int(db.execute(
            sa.select(sa.func.count(CreditEntry.id))).scalar_one())
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/{subscription['id']}/test")

    rows = _delivery_rows(user_id)
    assert len(rows) == 1
    event = rows[0]
    assert event.event_type == webhook_console.EVENT_TEST
    assert event.job_id == ""
    assert "test event" in event.payload["data"]["message"].lower()

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert int(db.execute(
            sa.select(sa.func.count(Job.id))).scalar_one()) == jobs_before
        assert int(db.execute(
            sa.select(sa.func.count(CreditEntry.id))).scalar_one()) == ledger_before
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_a_test_event_goes_through_the_real_delivery_path(portal):
    """Otherwise it proves nothing about the wiring it is meant to prove."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    subscription = _subscribe(portal, token)
    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/{subscription['id']}/test")

    sent = []

    def _sender(sub, delivery, **kwargs):
        sent.append((sub.url, delivery.event_type, delivery.payload))
        return 200

    from platform_core.public_api import outbox

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        report = outbox.deliver_due(db, sender=_sender)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert report["delivered"] == 1
    assert sent and sent[0][0] == RECEIVER
    assert sent[0][1] == webhook_console.EVENT_TEST


# ── Rotation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_rotation_signs_with_both_secrets_during_the_grace_window(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    created = _subscribe(portal, token)
    old_secret = created["secret"]

    page = portal.get("/developers/webhooks").text
    response = portal.post(
        f"/developers/webhooks/{created['id']}/rotate",
        data={"csrf_token": _csrf(page)}, follow_redirects=False)
    # The secret must not travel in the URL: history, Referer and access logs
    # all keep query strings. It comes back on the next render, once.
    assert "secret=" not in response.headers["location"]
    shown = portal.get("/developers/webhooks").text
    new_secret = re.search(r"<code>([A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})</code>", shown).group(1)
    assert new_secret and new_secret != old_secret
    # …and it is gone on the next load.
    assert new_secret not in portal.get("/developers/webhooks").text

    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/{created['id']}/test")

    captured = {}

    def _sender(sub, delivery, **kwargs):
        from platform_core.public_api import delivery as delivery_mod
        captured["headers"] = delivery_mod.build_headers(sub, delivery)
        return 200

    from platform_core.public_api import outbox

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        outbox.deliver_due(db, sender=_sender)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    headers = captured["headers"]
    signature = headers[webhooks.SIGNATURE_HEADER]
    body = webhooks.canonical_body(_delivery_rows(user_id)[0].payload)
    stamp = int(headers[webhooks.TIMESTAMP_HEADER])
    event_id = headers[webhooks.EVENT_HEADER]
    # A receiver that already switched verifies…
    assert webhooks.verify(new_secret, timestamp=stamp, event_id=event_id,
                           body=body, signature=signature)
    # …and one that has not yet switched still verifies.
    assert webhooks.verify(old_secret, timestamp=stamp, event_id=event_id,
                           body=body, signature=signature)


def test_the_old_secret_stops_working_after_the_window(portal):
    _user_id, token = _account(portal)
    created = _subscribe(portal, token)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        subscription = db.get(WebhookSubscription, created["id"])
        webhook_console.rotate_secret(db, subscription)
        db.commit()
        assert webhook_console.grace_secret(subscription) is not None
        later = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + webhook_console.ROTATION_GRACE \
            + timedelta(minutes=1)
        assert webhook_console.grace_secret(subscription, now=later) is None
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── Disable ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_disabling_keeps_the_history_and_stops_new_events(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    created = _subscribe(portal, token)
    _job_id, _delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)
    before = len(_delivery_rows(user_id))

    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/{created['id']}/disable")

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        subscription = db.get(WebhookSubscription, created["id"])
        assert subscription is not None, "disabled, not deleted"
        assert subscription.enabled is False
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert len(_delivery_rows(user_id)) == before

    # A later job queues nothing for a disabled endpoint.
    _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)
    assert len(_delivery_rows(user_id)) == before


# ── SSRF regression ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@pytest.mark.parametrize("url", [
    "http://receiver.example.com/hook",     # plain http
    "https://127.0.0.1/hook",
    "https://[::1]/hook",
    "https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
])
def test_the_console_cannot_reach_an_internal_target(portal, url):
    """Every console operation ends in a request we make; the guard is the
    same one subscription creation uses, and it is checked again here."""
    _user_id, token = _account(portal)
    refused = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/webhooks", json={"url": url},
                          headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    assert refused.status_code == 400, url


def test_a_resend_revalidates_the_target_before_sending(portal, monkeypatch):
    """The URL was safe when it was registered; it is checked again on the way
    out, because DNS can be repointed after the fact."""
    from platform_core.public_api import delivery as delivery_mod

    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    _subscribe(portal, token)
    _job_id, delivery = _finished_job_with_delivery(portal, token, user_id)
    _post(portal, f"/developers/webhooks/deliveries/{delivery.id}/resend")

    seen = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        webhooks, "validate_target",
        lambda url, **kwargs: seen.append(url))
    try:
        delivery_mod.send_delivery(
            _subscription_of(user_id), _delivery_rows(user_id)[0],
            resolver=lambda host: ["203.0.113.10"])
    except Exception:                          # noqa: BLE001 - no real receiver
        pass
    assert seen and seen[0] == RECEIVER


def _subscription_of(user_id: str):
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        import sqlalchemy as sa
        return db.execute(sa.select(WebhookSubscription).where(
            WebhookSubscription.user_id == user_id)).scalars().first()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

"""EXT-11 — budgets, alerts and the D3 fix.

Three properties decide whether a budget feature is safe: it never writes to the
ledger, a hard cap refuses deterministically, and the alerts do not become noise.
Everything here tests one of those.

def _account(client, credits: int = 500):
    from platform_core import credit
    from platform_core.users import tao_nguoi_dung

    email = f"bg-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        user = tao_nguoi_dung(db, email=email, password="a-good-password-12")
        user.is_verified = True
        db.flush()
        credit.cap_tay(db, user.id, credits, by="test")
        db.commit()
        user_id = user.id
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    page = client.get("/login").text
    client.post("/login", data={"username": email,
                                "password": "a-good-password-12",
                                "csrf_token": _csrf(page)},
                follow_redirects=False)
    keys_page = client.get("/developers/keys").text
    created = client.post("/developers/keys",
                          data={"name": "budget", "csrf_token": _csrf(keys_page),
                                "scopes": list(SCOPES)})
    token = re.search(r"<code>(ltt_sk_[^<]+)</code>", created.text).group(1)
    return user_id, token


def _run(client, token, *, count: int = 1, key: str = ""):
    payload = {"topic": "budget", "count": count}
    quote = client.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": TOOL, "input": payload},
                        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    assert quote.status_code == 200, quote.text
    return client.post(
        f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs",
        json={"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote.json()["quote"], "input": payload},
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                 "Idempotency-Key": key or f"bg-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"})


def _ledger(user_id: str) -> list:
    import sqlalchemy as sa
    from platform_core.models import CreditEntry

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        return [(row.kind, row.delta) for row in db.execute(
            sa.select(CreditEntry).where(CreditEntry.user_id == user_id)
            .order_by(CreditEntry.id)).scalars().all()]
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── The D3 fix: the ceiling counts API spending only ────────────────────────

def test_web_spending_does_not_consume_the_api_allowance(portal):
    """The defect EXT-01 found and D3 decided: a customer using the web app
    could exhaust the daily allowance that exists to bound a leaked API key."""
    from platform_core import credit

    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201        # 5 credits via the API

    # A job created the way the UI creates one: no API meta on its params.
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        from platform_core.job_submit import submit_with_credit

        submit_with_credit(db, user_id=user_id, app_slug="thumbnail",
                           job_type="thumbnail.generate",
                           params={"topic": "made in the ui", "count": 4,
                                   "owner_id": user_id})
        db.commit()
        since = budgets.window_start(budgets.PERIOD_DAY)
        api_only = budgets.api_spend_since(db, user_id=user_id, since=since)
        everything = -sum(
            delta for kind, delta in _ledger(user_id) if delta < 0)
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    assert api_only == 5, "only the API job counts"
    assert everything > api_only, "the UI job did spend, it just is not counted"
    assert credit.so_du(*_balance_args(user_id)) >= 0


def _balance_args(user_id: str):
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        from platform_core import credit

        return db, user_id
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── Hard caps ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_a_hard_cap_refuses_the_call_that_would_cross_it(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=10, period="day",
                       hard_cap=True)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201        # 5 of 10
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201        # 10 of 10
    refused = _run(portal, token)                        # would be 15
    assert refused.status_code == 429
    body = refused.json()
    assert body["code"] == "quota_exceeded"
    # The refusal names which rule applied — otherwise every support
    # conversation about a 429 starts with an investigation.
    assert body["source"] == "budget" and body["limit"] == 10


def test_a_soft_budget_never_refuses_anything(portal):
    """Somebody who asked to be *told* at 80% must not be silently stopped."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=10, period="day",
                       hard_cap=False)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    for _ in range(4):
        assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201    # 20 credits, over 10


def test_the_stricter_of_operator_and_customer_wins(portal):
    user_id, _token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=1000, period="day",
                       hard_cap=True)
        db.commit()
        # The operator allows less than the customer asked for.
        cap = budgets.effective_cap(db, user_id=user_id, operator_daily=50)
        assert cap["limit"] == 50 and cap["source"] == "operator"
        # …and the other way around.
        cap = budgets.effective_cap(db, user_id=user_id, operator_daily=5000)
        assert cap["limit"] == 1000 and cap["source"] == "budget"
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_a_budget_never_writes_to_the_ledger(portal):
    """The property that makes a self-service field safe to put near money."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201
    before = _ledger(user_id)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budget = budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=10, period="day",
                                hard_cap=True)
        db.commit()
        budgets.status(db, budget)
        alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    assert _ledger(user_id) == before


def test_a_replayed_call_is_not_counted_twice(portal):
    """Idempotent replay must not look like a second purchase to a budget."""
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    payload = {"topic": "budget", "count": 1}
    quote = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/quotes",
                        json={"tool": TOOL, "input": payload},
                        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}).json()
    body = {"tool": TOOL, "quote": quote["quote"], "input": payload}
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
               "Idempotency-Key": f"bg-replay-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"}

    first = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs", json=body, headers=headers)
    assert first.status_code == 201
    # The identical request again — which is what a client retrying a timeout
    # sends, and the only thing that counts as a replay.
    again = portal.post(f"{API_V1_PREFIX}/jobs", json=body, headers=headers)
    assert again.status_code == 200 and again.json()["id"] == first.json()["id"]

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        spent = budgets.api_spend_since(
            db, user_id=user_id, since=budgets.window_start("day"))
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert spent == 5


def test_a_project_budget_only_counts_that_project(portal):
    from platform_core.public_api import projects

    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        other = projects.create(db, user_id=user_id, name="Elsewhere")
        db.commit()
        since = budgets.window_start("day")
        assert budgets.api_spend_since(db, user_id=user_id, since=since,
                                       project_id=other.id) == 0
        assert budgets.api_spend_since(db, user_id=user_id, since=since) == 5
    finally:
        _close(gen)


# ── Alerts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _alerts(user_id: str) -> list:
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        return notifications.list_for(db, user_id=user_id)
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def test_crossing_a_threshold_raises_one_alert_not_many(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=10, period="day")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201        # 5 of 10 = 50%

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        first = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
        again = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    kinds = [row.kind for row in first]
    assert notifications.BUDGET_THRESHOLD in kinds
    assert again == [], "the same condition must not alert twice in cooldown"


def test_each_threshold_is_its_own_news(portal):
    user_id, token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=user_id, amount=10, period="day")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    _run(portal, token)                                   # 50%
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    _run(portal, token)                                   # 100%
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        raised = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert any(row.kind == notifications.BUDGET_EXCEEDED for row in raised)


def test_a_low_balance_is_raised_once_a_day(portal):
    user_id, _token = _account(portal, credits=5)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        first = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
        second = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
        assert any(row.kind == notifications.LOW_CREDIT for row in first)
        assert second == []
        # …and again once the cooldown has passed.
        later = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=2)
        third = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id, now=later)
        db.commit()
        assert any(row.kind == notifications.LOW_CREDIT for row in third)
    finally:
        _close(gen)

                      env={devkeys.PEPPER_ENV: PEPPER})

    finally:

def test_a_dead_webhook_endpoint_is_reported(portal):
    from platform_core.public_api.tables import (WEBHOOK_DEAD, WebhookDelivery,
                                                 WebhookSubscription)
    from platform_core import secretbox

    user_id, _token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        subscription = WebhookSubscription(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()), user_id=user_id, url="https://example.com/x",
            secret_enc=secretbox.ma_hoa("s" * 32), events=[], enabled=True,
            created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        db.add(subscription)
        for index in range(alerting.DEAD_DELIVERY_THRESHOLD):
            db.add(WebhookDelivery(
                id=str(uuid.uuid4()), subscription_id=subscription.id,
                user_id=user_id, event_id=f"e{index}", event_type="job.succeeded",
                payload={}, status=WEBHOOK_DEAD, attempts=6,
                next_attempt_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
                created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc)))
        db.commit()
        raised = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert any(row.kind == notifications.WEBHOOK_FAILING for row in raised)


def test_only_money_and_credentials_are_worth_an_email():
    for kind in (notifications.LOW_CREDIT, notifications.BUDGET_EXCEEDED,
                 notifications.KEY_EXPIRING):
        assert kind in notifications.EMAIL_KINDS
    # A threshold the customer set to be informed by is not an interruption.
    assert notifications.BUDGET_THRESHOLD not in notifications.EMAIL_KINDS


def test_an_email_failure_does_not_lose_the_alert(portal):
    class _Broken:
        def send(self, email):
            raise RuntimeError("smtp is down")

    user_id, _token = _account(portal, credits=1)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        raised = alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
        row = next(item for item in raised
                   if item.kind == notifications.LOW_CREDIT)
        assert notifications.send_email_for(db, row, mailer=_Broken()) is False
    finally:
        _close(gen)
    assert any(item.kind == notifications.LOW_CREDIT
               for item in _alerts(user_id))

@pytest.mark.parametrize("amount", [0, 5, -100, "abc"])

def test_thresholds_are_bounded(portal):
    with pytest.raises(budgets.BudgetError):
        budgets.normalize_thresholds([3])
    with pytest.raises(budgets.BudgetError):
        budgets.normalize_thresholds([150])
    assert budgets.normalize_thresholds([80, 50, 50]) == [50, 80]


def test_one_account_never_sees_another_accounts_budget_or_alerts(portal):
    first_id, _token = _account(portal)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        budgets.create(db, user_id=first_id, amount=99, period="day")
        notifications.raise_alert(db, user_id=first_id,
                                  kind=notifications.LOW_CREDIT,
                                  subject="balance", title="AliceOnlyAlert")
        db.commit()
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    portal.post("/logout", data={}, follow_redirects=False)
    second_id, _token = _account(portal)
    assert "AliceOnlyAlert" not in portal.get("/developers/notifications").text

    # Asserting on the *state* the second account should be in, not on the
    # absence of a substring. The earlier version looked for "99" inside the
    # budget card — a region that also renders the account's project ids, and a
    # uuid contains "99" about one time in nine. It passed on luck and failed a
    # full-suite run for a reason that had nothing to do with tenant isolation.
    card = _budget_cell(portal.get("/developers/usage").text)
    assert card, "the budget card should render even with no budget set"
    assert "Chưa đặt ngân sách nào." in card
    assert "Ngưỡng cảnh báo" not in card, "somebody else's budget table rendered"

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert budgets.list_for(db, user_id=second_id) == []
        assert len(budgets.list_for(db, user_id=first_id)) == 1
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _budget_cell(html: str) -> str:
    """The budget card only — up to the end of its own `div.card`.

    Anchored on the next card rather than on the first `</div>`, which used to
    stop early or run long depending on markup nobody thought was load-bearing.
    """
    match = re.search(r'Ngân sách của bạn.*?(?=<div class="card">|\Z)', html,
                      re.S)
    return match.group(0) if match else ""

def test_a_budget_can_be_created_and_deleted_from_the_page(portal):
    user_id, _token = _account(portal)
    page = portal.get("/developers/usage").text
    portal.post("/developers/budgets",
                data={"amount": "250", "period": "month", "project_id": "",
                      "hard_cap": "1", "csrf_token": _csrf(page)},
                follow_redirects=False)

    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        rows = budgets.list_for(db, user_id=user_id)
        assert len(rows) == 1 and rows[0].amount == 250
        assert rows[0].hard_cap is True
        budget_id = rows[0].id
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    page = portal.get("/developers/usage").text
    assert "250" in page
    portal.post(f"/developers/budgets/{budget_id}/delete",
                data={"csrf_token": _csrf(page)}, follow_redirects=False)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert budgets.list_for(db, user_id=user_id) == []
    finally:
        _close(gen)


def _usage_rows(html: str) -> str:
    """Just the results table: the filter dropdown lists every tool whatever
    the filter is, so searching the whole page proves nothing."""
    match = re.search(r"Chi tiêu theo lời gọi.*?</table>", html, re.S)
    if not match:
        return ""
    body = re.search(r"<tbody>.*?</tbody>", match.group(0), re.S)
    return body.group(0) if body else ""


def test_the_usage_page_filters_by_tool_key_and_status(portal):
    _user_id, token = _account(portal)
    assert _run(portal, token).status_code == 201

    assert TOOL in _usage_rows(portal.get(f"/developers/usage?tool={TOOL}").text)
    assert TOOL not in _usage_rows(
        portal.get("/developers/usage?tool=image.generate").text)
    # The job is queued, not succeeded, so filtering on succeeded empties it.
    assert TOOL not in _usage_rows(
        portal.get("/developers/usage?status=succeeded").text)
    assert TOOL in _usage_rows(
        portal.get("/developers/usage?status=queued").text)


def test_the_notifications_page_marks_everything_read(portal):
    user_id, _token = _account(portal, credits=1)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        alerting.scan_account(db, user_id=user_id)
        db.commit()
        assert notifications.unread_count(db, user_id=user_id) >= 1
    finally:
        _close(gen)

    page = portal.get("/developers/notifications").text
    portal.post("/developers/notifications/read",
                data={"csrf_token": _csrf(page)}, follow_redirects=False)
    gen, db = _session()
    try:
        assert notifications.unread_count(db, user_id=user_id) == 0
    finally:
        _close(gen)

"""EXT-12 — test mode: the whole API, with the provider replaced.

What is being defended here is a pair of claims a developer has to be able to
trust without reading our code:

* a test key **cannot** spend. Not "spends little" — the ledger is never
  touched, so a leaked test key costs nothing;
* live and test **never mix**. A test key sees only test work; a live key sees
  only live work, and neither can read, cancel or download the other's.

And one claim that keeps the sandbox honest: the response shape is the tool's
published contract, not a hand-written mock. A sandbox whose shape drifts from
production teaches an integration to parse something that will never arrive.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import time
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from platform_core.public_api import (keys as devkeys, limits, sandbox,
                                      webhooks)
from server.api.inventory import API_V1_PREFIX

PEPPER = "sandbox-test-pepper-" + "s" * 40
TOOL = "image.thumbnail"
SCOPES = ("tools:read", "jobs:create", "jobs:read", "jobs:cancel",
          "artifacts:read", "webhooks:manage")
INPUT = {"topic": "sandbox", "count": 1}
RECEIVER = "https://receiver.example.com/hook"

#: Every provider call the fixture saw. A test job must add nothing to it.
PROVIDER_CALLS: list = []

    """Resolve the test receiver without depending on somebody else's DNS."""
    if host.endswith("example.com"):
        return ["93.184.216.34"]
    raise OSError(f"unknown test host: {host}")

    monkeypatch.setenv("LTT_DATA_DIR", str(tmp_path / "data"))

    monkeypatch.setenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "stub-key-not-used")
    limits.reset()

    import platform_core.db as dbmod
    import platform_core.storage as storage_mod

    storage_mod.set_storage(storage_mod.LocalStorage(str(tmp_path / "files")))

    Base.metadata.create_all(get_engine())
